bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第113卷 卷第一百一十三 。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government, Volume 113, scroll number one hundred thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 113.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀三十五】 起昭陽單閼，盡閼逢執徐，凡二年。。

translations.literal: 【Jin Records 35】 Beginning from Zhaoyang Dan'e through Yufeng Zhixu—in all, two years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Jin Records 35】 From the year Zhaoyang Dan'e through Yufeng Zhixu—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝戊元興二年（癸卯，公元四零三年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor An, in the second year of Yuanxing of the wu cycle (guimao, AD 403).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An of Jin, second year of Yuanxing (guimao, AD 403).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，盧循使司馬徐道覆寇東陽；

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Lu Xun sent his chief of staff Xu Daofu to raid Dongyang;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Lu Xun dispatched his chief of staff Xu Daofu to attack Dongyang;

sentences.zh: 二月，辛丑，建武將軍劉裕擊破之。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day xinchou, General Jianwu Liu Yu attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinchou day, General Jianwu Liu Yu routed them.

sentences.zh: 道覆，循之姊夫也。。

translations.literal: Daofu was Lu Xun's elder sister's husband.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu was Lu Xun's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以太尉玄為大將軍。。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the Grand Marshal Xuan was made Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day, Grand Marshal Huan Xuan was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，玄殺冀州刺史孫無終。。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Xuan killed Sun Wuzhong, Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day, Huan Xuan executed Sun Wuzhong, regional inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 玄上表請帥諸軍掃平關、洛，既而諷朝廷下詔不許，乃云：「奉詔故止。」

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial requesting to lead the armies to sweep clear Guan and Luo; then he prompted the court to issue an edict refusing permission, and then said: "I cease because I received the command."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan memorialized the throne asking to lead all armies to pacify the Guan and Luo regions; he then maneuvered the court into issuing an edict denying the request, and declared, "I halt only because I have received the imperial command."

sentences.zh: 玄初欲飭裝，先命作輕舸，載服玩、書畫。

translations.literal: When Xuan first intended to prepare his baggage, he first ordered light boats made to carry clothing, curios, books, and paintings.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan first set about preparing for the campaign, he had light skiffs built in advance to carry his robes, curios, books, and paintings.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，玄曰：「兵凶戰危，脫有意外，當使輕而易運。」

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Xuan said: "War is inauspicious and battle is perilous; if there should be an unforeseen event, they should be made light and easy to transport."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why, he replied, "War is cruel and battle uncertain; should anything go wrong, these must be light enough to move quickly."

sentences.zh: 眾皆笑之。。

translations.literal: All laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸巳朔，日有食之。。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day of the cycle guisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on the first day of the month (guisi), the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 南燕主備德故吏趙融自長安來，始得母兄凶問，備德號慟吐血，因而寢疾。。

translations.literal: Zhao Rong, a former subordinate of the lord of Southern Yan, Murong De, came from Chang'an; only then did he receive news of the violent deaths of his mother and elder brother. Murong De wailed and spat blood, and consequently took to his bed ill.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Rong, once an official under Murong De of Southern Yan, arrived from Chang'an with word that the ruler's mother and elder brother had been killed. Murong De cried out in grief until he vomited blood and fell seriously ill.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉慕容達謀反，遣牙門皇璆帥眾攻端門，殿中帥侯赤眉開門應之；

translations.literal: Murong Da, Colonel of the Masters of Writing, plotted rebellion; he sent the gate officer Huang Qiu to lead troops to attack the Duan Gate, and the palace guard Hou Chimei opened the gate in response;
translations.idiomatic: Murong Da, metropolitan commandant, plotted rebellion and sent gate officer Huang Qiu at the head of troops to storm the Duan Gate; palace guard Hou Chimei opened the gate from within in collusion;

sentences.zh: 中黃門孫進扶備德逾城匿於進捨。

translations.literal: the palace attendant Sun Jin supported Murong De over the wall and hid him in Jin's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: palace attendant Sun Jin helped Murong De over the wall and concealed him in his own house.

sentences.zh: 段宏等聞宮中有變，勒兵屯四門。

translations.literal: Duan Hong and others, hearing that there was trouble within the palace, drew up troops and encamped at the four gates.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the disturbance in the palace, Duan Hong and others mustered troops and held the four city gates.

sentences.zh: 備德入宮，誅赤眉等。

translations.literal: Murong De entered the palace and executed Chimei and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De re-entered the palace and executed Hou Chimei and his accomplices.

sentences.zh: 達出奔魏。。

translations.literal: Da fled abroad to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Da fled to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 備德優遷徙之民，使之長復不役；

translations.literal: Murong De showed favor to resettled commoners, making them permanently exempt from corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Murong De granted favorable treatment to resettled households, exempting them permanently from labor service;

sentences.zh: 民緣此迭相廕冒，或百室合戶，或千丁共籍，以避課役。

translations.literal: because of this the people in turn shielded one another in fraud; some hundred households joined into one register, or a thousand adult males shared one household roll, to evade tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: commoners then shielded one another in fraud—sometimes a hundred households merged into one register, sometimes a thousand adult males shared a single household roll—to escape taxation and corvée.

sentences.zh: 尚書韓言卓請加隱核，備德從之，使言卓巡行郡縣，得廕戶五萬八千。。

translations.literal: the Minister of the Masters of Writing Han Yanzhuo requested intensified hidden-household audits; Murong De assented and sent Yanzhuo on circuit through the commanderies and counties, uncovering fifty-eight thousand shielded households.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Han Yanzhuo urged stricter audits of concealed households; Murong De agreed and sent him on circuit through the commanderies and counties, where he uncovered fifty-eight thousand hidden households.

sentences.zh: 泰山賊王始聚眾數萬，自稱太平皇帝，署置公卿；

translations.literal: the bandit of Mount Tai Wang Shi gathered a host of tens of thousands, styled himself Emperor Taiping, and appointed dukes and ministers;
translations.idiomatic: The Mount Tai bandit Wang Shi raised a force of tens of thousands, proclaimed himself Emperor Taiping, and appointed his own ministers of state;

sentences.zh: 南燕桂林王鎮討禽之。

translations.literal: the Prince of Guilin of Southern Yan, Murong Zhen, campaigned against him and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zhen, Prince of Guilin of Southern Yan, campaigned against him and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，或問其父及兄弟安在，始曰：「太上皇蒙塵於外，征東、征西為亂兵所害。」

translations.literal: At the time of execution, someone asked where his father and brothers were; Shi said: "The retired emperor suffers exile abroad; the eastern and western campaigners were killed by mutinous troops."
translations.idiomatic: As he faced execution, someone asked where his father and brothers were; Wang Shi replied, "The retired emperor languishes in exile abroad; the eastern and western campaigners were slain by mutinous troops."

sentences.zh: 其妻怒之曰：「君正坐此口，奈何尚爾！」

translations.literal: His wife angrily said to him: "You are being executed precisely because of this mouth—how can you still go on like this!"
translations.idiomatic: His wife snapped at him, "It is precisely because of that mouth that you stand here—how can you still talk like this!"

sentences.zh: 始曰：「皇后不知，自古豈有不亡之國！

translations.literal: Shi said: "The empress does not understand—from antiquity has there ever been a state that did not perish!
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The empress does not understand—from antiquity onward, has any state ever failed to fall!

sentences.zh: 朕則崩矣，終不改號！」。

translations.literal: I am about to die, but I will never change my title!"
translations.idiomatic: I am about to die, but I will never renounce my imperial title!"

sentences.zh: 五月，燕王熙作龍騰苑，方十餘里，役徒二萬人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Yan king Murong Xi built the Dragon Soaring Park, more than ten li square, employing twenty thousand laborers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Murong Xi of Northern Yan built the Dragon Soaring Park, more than ten li on a side, with twenty thousand laborers pressed into service.

sentences.zh: 築景雲山於苑內，基廣五百步，峰高十七丈。。

translations.literal: Within the park he constructed Mount Jingyun; its base was five hundred paces wide and its peak seventeen zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the park he raised Mount Jingyun, five hundred paces wide at the base and seventeen zhang at the summit.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊子，魏主珪北巡，作離宮於豺山。。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day wuzi, the lord of Wei, Tuoba Gui, toured north and built a detached palace on Mount Chai.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on wuzi day, Emperor Daowu of Northern Wei toured the north and built a detached palace on Mount Chai.

sentences.zh: 平原太守和跋奢豪喜名，珪惡而殺之，使其弟毘等就與訣。

translations.literal: He Ba, governor of Pingyuan, was extravagant and fond of reputation; Gui hated this and killed him, sending his younger brothers Pi and others to take leave of him.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba, governor of Pingyuan, was extravagant and hungry for fame; Tuoba Gui detested this and had him executed, but allowed his younger brothers Pi and the rest to visit him for a final farewell.

sentences.zh: 跋曰：「灅北土瘠，可遷水南，勉為主計。」

translations.literal: Ba said: "North of the Rao the soil is poor; you may move south of the river—strive to plan for our lord."
translations.idiomatic: He Ba told them, "The land north of the Rao is poor; move south of the river and do your best to serve our lord."

sentences.zh: 且使之背己，曰：「汝何忍視吾之死也！」

translations.literal: Moreover he made them turn their backs to him, saying: "How can you bear to watch my death!"
translations.idiomatic: Then he made them turn their backs to him, saying, "How can you bear to watch me die!"

sentences.zh: 毘等諭其意，詐稱使者，逃入秦。

translations.literal: Pi and the others understood his intent; they falsely claimed to be envoys and fled into Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Pi and the others understood his meaning; posing as envoys, they fled into Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 珪怒，滅其家。

translations.literal: Gui was enraged and exterminated their clan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui flew into a rage and exterminated the entire He clan.

sentences.zh: 中壘將軍鄧淵從弟尚書暉與跋善，或譖諸珪曰：「毘之出亡，暉實送之。」

translations.literal: Deng Yuan, General of the Central Ramparts, had a younger cousin, the Master of Writing Hui, who was on good terms with Ba; someone slandered them to Gui, saying: "Pi's flight abroad—Hui in fact sent him off."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuan, general of the central ramparts, had a cousin, Master of Writing Deng Hui, who was close to He Ba; someone slandered them to Tuoba Gui, saying, "It was Hui who actually helped Pi escape."

sentences.zh: 珪疑淵知其謀，賜淵死。。

translations.literal: Gui suspected that Yuan knew of the plot and granted Yuan death.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui suspected that Deng Yuan had known of the plot and ordered him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 南涼王辱檀及沮渠蒙遜互出兵攻呂隆，隆患之。

translations.literal: The lord of Southern Liang, Tufa Rutan, and Juqu Mengxun each sent out troops to attack Lü Long; Long was distressed by this.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan of Southern Liang and Juqu Mengxun repeatedly sent troops against Lü Long, who was hard pressed by the attacks.

sentences.zh: 秦之謀臣言於秦王興曰：「隆藉先世之資，專制河外，今雖饑窘，尚能自支，若將來豐贍，終不為吾有。

translations.literal: A strategist of Qin said to the king of Qin, Yao Xing: "Long relies on his forebears' resources and holds sole sway beyond the river; though he is now hungry and straitened, he can still sustain himself—if in the future he becomes rich and ample, in the end he will not be ours.
translations.idiomatic: A Later Qin strategist told King Yao Xing, "Lü Long rests on his forebears' legacy and rules the lands beyond the river alone; though he is now starving and cornered, he can still hold out—and if he ever prospers again, he will never truly be ours.

sentences.zh: 涼州險絕，土田饒沃，不如因其危而取之。」

translations.literal: Liang Province is perilously defensible and its fields rich and fertile—it would be better to take it while he is in danger."
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou is rugged and its fields fertile; we should seize it while he is in peril."

sentences.zh: 興乃遣使征呂超入侍。

translations.literal: Xing thereupon sent envoys summoning Lü Chao to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing then sent envoys summoning Lü Chao to attend at the Qin court.

sentences.zh: 隆念姑臧終無以自存，乃因超請迎於秦。

translations.literal: Long, reflecting that Guzang could not ultimately preserve itself, thereupon had Chao request to be received in Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Guzang could not survive on its own, Lü Long had Chao ask to surrender the state to Qin.

sentences.zh: 興遣尚書左僕射齊難、鎮西將軍姚詰、左王乞伏乾歸、鎮遠將軍趙曜帥步騎四萬迎隆於河西，南涼王辱檀攝昌松、魏安二戍以避之。

translations.literal: Xing dispatched the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Qi Nan, the General Who Pacifies the West Yao Jie, the Left King Qifu Gangui, and the General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhao Yao to lead forty thousand foot and horse to receive Long on the west of the river; the lord of Southern Liang, Tufa Rutan, withdrew from the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent Left Vice Director Qi Nan, General Who Pacifies the West Yao Jie, Left King Qifu Gangui, and General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhao Yao at the head of forty thousand infantry and cavalry to receive Lü Long west of the Yellow River; Tufa Rutan of Southern Liang pulled back from the garrisons of Changsong and Wei'an to give them room.

sentences.zh: 八月，齊難等至姑臧，隆素車白馬迎於道旁。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qi Nan and the others reached Guzang; Long, in an unadorned cart and white horse, received them by the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Qi Nan and his force reached Guzang; Lü Long met them by the roadside in a plain cart drawn by a white horse.

sentences.zh: 隆勸難擊沮渠蒙遜，蒙遜使臧莫孩拒之，敗其前軍。

translations.literal: Long urged Nan to attack Juqu Mengxun; Mengxun sent Zang Mohai to resist and defeated their vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Long urged Qi Nan to attack Juqu Mengxun; Mengxun sent Zang Mohai to block him and routed the Qin vanguard.

sentences.zh: 難乃與蒙遜結盟，蒙遜遣弟挐入貢於秦。

translations.literal: Nan thereupon allied with Mengxun; Mengxun sent his younger brother Ju to present tribute to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan then made peace with Mengxun, who sent his younger brother Ju to present tribute at the Qin court.

sentences.zh: 難以司馬王尚行涼州刺史，配兵三千鎮姑臧，以將軍閻松為倉松太守，郭將為番禾太守，分戍二城，徙隆宗族、僚屬及民萬戶於長安，興以隆為散騎常侍，超為安定太守，自餘文武隨才擢敘。。

translations.literal: Nan appointed the Chief of Staff Wang Shang acting Inspector of Liang Province, assigning three thousand troops to garrison Guzang; he made the general Yan Song governor of Cangsong and Guo Jiang governor of Fanhe, dividing garrisons between the two cities; he moved Long's clansmen, staff, and ten thousand households of commoners to Chang'an; Xing made Long Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and Chao governor of Anding; the remaining civil and military officers were promoted according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Nan installed Chief of Staff Wang Shang as acting regional inspector of Liangzhou with three thousand troops to hold Guzang; generals Yan Song and Guo Jiang were made governors of Cangsong and Fanhe respectively, each guarding a city; Lü Long's kin, officials, and ten thousand households were relocated to Chang'an; Yao Xing made Lü Long regular attendant within the yellow gates and Lü Chao governor of Anding, while the rest of the civil and military officers were appointed according to merit.

sentences.zh: 初，郭黁常言「代呂者王」，故其起兵，先推王詳，後推王乞基；

translations.literal: Earlier, Guo Nen had often said, "He who replaces Lü will be Wang"; therefore when he raised troops he first advanced Wang Xiang, then Wang Qiji;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guo Nen had prophesied that "the one who replaces the Lü will be a Wang"; when he raised troops he first set up Wang Xiang, then Wang Qiji as figureheads;

sentences.zh: 及隆東遷，王尚卒代之。

translations.literal: when Long moved east, Wang Shang at last replaced them.
translations.idiomatic: and when Lü Long departed eastward, Wang Shang at last fulfilled the prophecy.

sentences.zh: 黁從乞伏乾歸降秦，以為滅秦者晉也，遂來奔，秦人追得，殺之。。

translations.literal: Nen followed Qifu Gangui in surrendering to Qin; believing that the one who would destroy Qin was Jin, he then came in flight; the men of Qin pursued and caught him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Nen followed Qifu Gangui in submitting to Qin, then decided that Jin would be Qin's destroyer and fled toward the east; Qin pursuers overtook and executed him.

sentences.zh: 沮渠蒙遜伯父中田護軍親信、臨松太守孔篤，皆驕恣為民患，蒙遜曰：「亂吾法者，二伯父也。」

translations.literal: Juqu Mengxun's paternal uncles, the Protector of the Army of Zhongtian Qinxin and the governor of Linsong Kong Du, were both arrogant and willful and a scourge to the people; Mengxun said: "Those who disrupt my laws are my two uncles."
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Mengxun's uncles Qinxin, protector of the army of Zhongtian, and Kong Du, governor of Linsong, were both arrogant tyrants who preyed on the people; Mengxun declared, "The men who wreck my laws are my two uncles."

sentences.zh: 皆逼之使自殺。。

translations.literal: He compelled both to kill themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He forced both to take their own lives.

sentences.zh: 秦遣使者梁構至張掖，蒙遜問曰：「禿髮辱檀為公而身為侯，何也？」

translations.literal: Qin sent the envoy Liang Gou to Zhangye; Mengxun asked: "Tufa Rutan is made a duke while I am made a marquis—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin sent envoy Liang Gou to Zhangye; Mengxun asked, "Why is Tufa Rutan made a duke while I am only a marquis?"

sentences.zh: 構曰：「辱檀凶狡，款誠未著，故朝廷以重爵虛名羈縻之。

translations.literal: Gou said: "Rutan is fierce and cunning; his sincere submission has not yet been made clear—therefore the court uses a heavy rank and empty title to tether him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gou replied, "Tufa Rutan is treacherous and his loyalty is still in doubt, so the court uses a grand but hollow title to keep him on a leash.

sentences.zh: 將軍忠貫白日，當入贊帝室，豈可以不信相待也！

translations.literal: The general's loyalty pierces the white sun; he should enter to assist the imperial house—how can one treat him with distrust!
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty shines as bright as the sun; you are fit to serve at the imperial center—how could the court treat you with suspicion!

sentences.zh: 聖朝爵必稱功，如尹緯、姚晃，佐命之臣，齊難、徐洛，一時猛將，爵皆不過侯伯，將軍何以先之乎！

translations.literal: In the sage court ranks must match merit—as with Yin Wei and Yao Huang, ministers who aided the mandate, or Qi Nan and Xu Luo, fierce generals of the age—their ranks were none higher than marquis or earl; why should the general go before them!
translations.idiomatic: In our sage court, rank must match merit—ministers such as Yin Wei and Yao Huang who aided the founding, or fierce generals such as Qi Nan and Xu Luo, hold no rank above marquis or earl; why should you rank ahead of them!

sentences.zh: 昔竇融殷勤固讓，不欲居舊臣之右，不意將軍忽有此問！」

translations.literal: In former times Dou Rong earnestly and firmly declined, unwilling to stand above old ministers—who would have thought the general would suddenly have this question!"
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Dou Rong firmly declined honors rather than stand above older ministers—I never expected you to raise this question!"

sentences.zh: 蒙遜曰：「朝廷何不即封張掖而更遠封西海邪？」

translations.literal: Mengxun said: "Why does the court not enfeoff Zhangye at once but instead enfeoff the distant Western Sea?"
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun retorted, "If the court trusts me, why not enfeoff Zhangye itself rather than some distant Western Sea domain?"

sentences.zh: 構曰：「張掖，將軍已自有之，所以遠授西海者，欲廣大將軍之國耳。」

translations.literal: Gou said: "Zhangye the general already possesses in his own right; the reason for granting the distant Western Sea from afar is to enlarge the general's state."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gou answered, "You already hold Zhangye in your own right; the distant Western Sea grant is meant to enlarge your domain."

sentences.zh: 蒙遜悅，乃受命。。

translations.literal: Mengxun was pleased and thereupon accepted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Mengxun was satisfied and accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓偉卒，大將軍玄以桓修代之。

translations.literal: Huan Wei, Inspector of Jing Province, died; the Grand General Xuan replaced him with Huan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wei, regional inspector of Jing Province, died; Grand General Huan Xuan appointed Huan Xiu in his place.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎曹靖之說玄曰：「謙、修兄弟專據內外，權勢太重。」

translations.literal: the Attendant Gentleman Cao Jingzhi advised Xuan, saying: "The brothers Qian and Xiu monopolize inner and outer power; their authority is too heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant gentleman Cao Jingzhi warned Huan Xuan, "The brothers Qian and Xiu hold sway inside and outside the government—their power is excessive."

sentences.zh: 玄乃以南郡相桓石康為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon made Huan Shikang, Administrator of Nan Commandery, Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan then made Huan Shikang, administrator of Nan Commandery, regional inspector of Jing Province instead.

sentences.zh: 石康，豁之子也。。

translations.literal: Shikang was the son of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shikang was a son of Huan Huo.

sentences.zh: 劉裕破盧循於永嘉，追至晉安，屢破之，循浮海南走。。

translations.literal: Liu Yu defeated Lu Xun at Yongjia, pursued to Jin'an, repeatedly defeated him, and Xun fled south by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu defeated Lu Xun at Yongjia, pursued him to Jin'an, and routed him repeatedly until Xun fled south by sea.

sentences.zh: 何無忌潛詣裕，勸裕於山陰起兵討桓玄。

translations.literal: He Wuji secretly visited Yu and urged Yu to raise troops at Shanyin to campaign against Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji secretly visited Liu Yu and urged him to raise troops at Shanyin to overthrow Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 裕謀於土豪孔靖，靖曰：「山陰去都道遠，舉事難成；

translations.literal: Yu consulted the local magnate Kong Jing; Jing said: "Shanyin is far from the capital on the road; raising the affair would be hard to accomplish;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu consulted local magnate Kong Jing, who said, "Shanyin is far from the capital and an uprising there would be hard to sustain;

sentences.zh: 且玄未篡位，不如待其已篡，於京口圖之。」

translations.literal: moreover Xuan has not yet usurped the throne—it would be better to wait until he has usurped it and plot at Jingkou."
translations.idiomatic: moreover, Huan Xuan has not yet seized the throne—better to wait until he has usurped it, then strike from Jingkou."

sentences.zh: 裕從之，靖，愉之孫也。。

translations.literal: Yu followed this; Jing was the grandson of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu agreed; Kong Jing was a grandson of Kong Yu.

sentences.zh: 九月，魏主珪如南平城，規度灅南，將建新都。。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the lord of Wei, Gui, went to Nanpingcheng, surveyed south of the Rao, and intended to build a new capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Tuoba Gui went to Nanpingcheng, surveyed the lands south of the Rao River, and planned a new capital.

sentences.zh: 侍中殷仲文、散騎常侍卞范之勸大將軍玄早受禪，陰撰九錫文及冊命。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Yin Zhongwen and the Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates Bian Fanzhi urged the Grand General Xuan to accept the abdication early; in secret they drafted the text of the Nine Bestowals and the investiture mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Yin Zhongwen and regular attendant Bian Fanzhi urged Grand General Huan Xuan to seize the throne quickly; in secret they drafted the Nine Bestowals document and the investiture edict.

sentences.zh: 以桓謙為侍中、開府、錄尚書事，王謐為中書監、領司徒，桓胤為中書令，加桓修撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He made Huan Qian Palace Attendant, Opener of the Mansion, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Wang Mi Supervisor of the Palace Writers and concurrent Minister of Education; Huan Yin Palace Writer-in-Chief; and added to Huan Xiu the rank General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Huan Qian palace attendant with an opening office and recorder of the Masters of Writing; Wang Mi supervisor of the palace writers and concurrent minister of education; Huan Yin palace writer-in-chief; and promoted Huan Xiu to general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 胤，沖之孫也。

translations.literal: Yin was the grandson of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yin was a grandson of Huan Chong.

sentences.zh: 丙子，冊命玄為相國，總百揆，封十郡，為楚王，加九錫，楚國置丞相以下官。。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, the investiture mandate made Xuan Chancellor of State, overseeing all affairs, enfeoffed him with ten commanderies as King of Chu, added the Nine Bestowals, and the state of Chu established offices from Chancellor of State downward.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day, an investiture edict made Huan Xuan chancellor of state with authority over all government affairs, enfeoffed him as King of Chu over ten commanderies, granted the Nine Bestowals, and authorized a full Chu state bureaucracy down from chancellor.

sentences.zh: 桓謙私問彭城內史劉裕曰：「楚王勳德隆重，朝廷之情，鹹謂宜有揖讓，卿以為何如？」

translations.literal: Huan Qian privately asked Liu Yu, Administrator of Pengcheng: "The King of Chu's merit and virtue are weighty; the sentiment at court all says there should be a yielding of the throne—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian privately asked Liu Yu, administrator of Pengcheng, "The King of Chu's achievements are towering, and court opinion widely favors abdication in his favor—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「楚王，宣武之子，勳德蓋世。

translations.literal: Yu said: "The King of Chu is the son of Xuanwu; his merit and virtue cover the age.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu answered, "The King of Chu is a son of Duke Huan Wen the Martial; his merit towers above the age.

sentences.zh: 晉室微弱，民望久移，乘運禪代，有何不可？」

translations.literal: The house of Jin is feeble; the people's expectation has long shifted—seizing the mandate to transfer the throne by abdication, what could not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house is feeble and popular allegiance has long shifted; to take the mandate by abdication—what could be wrong with that?"

sentences.zh: 謙喜曰：「卿謂之可即可耳。」。

translations.literal: Qian said in delight: "If you say it can be done, then it can be done—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian was delighted and said, "If you say it can be done, then so it shall be."

sentences.zh: 新野人庾仄，殷仲堪之黨也，聞桓偉死，石康未至，乃起兵襲雍州刺史馮該於襄陽，走之。

translations.literal: Yu Ze of Xinye, a partisan of Yin Zhongkan, hearing that Huan Wei had died and Shikang had not yet arrived, thereupon raised troops and attacked Feng Gai, Inspector of Yong Province, at Xiangyang, driving him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ze of Xinye, an ally of Yin Zhongkan, heard that Huan Wei was dead and Huan Shikang had not yet reached Jing Province; he raised troops and attacked regional inspector Feng Gai at Xiangyang, driving him from the city.

sentences.zh: 仄有眾七千，設壇，祭七廟，雲欲討桓玄，江陵震動。

translations.literal: Ze had a host of seven thousand; he set up an altar and sacrificed to the seven temples, declaring that he intended to campaign against Huan Xuan; Jiangling was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ze mustered seven thousand men, set up an altar, and sacrificed to the seven imperial temples, proclaiming that he would overthrow Huan Xuan; the whole Jiangling region was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 石康至州，發兵攻襄陽，仄敗，奔秦。。

translations.literal: When Shikang reached the province, he sent out troops to attack Xiangyang; Ze was defeated and fled to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Shikang reached his post, he marched on Xiangyang; Yu Ze was defeated and fled to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 高雅之表南燕主備德請伐桓玄曰：「縱未能廓清吳、會，亦可收江北之地。」

translations.literal: Gao Yazhi memorialized the lord of Southern Yan, Murong De, requesting a campaign against Huan Xuan, saying: "Even if we cannot entirely clear Wu and Kuaiji, we may still recover the lands north of the river."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yazhi memorialized Murong De of Southern Yan urging an attack on Huan Xuan: "Even if we cannot fully pacify Wu and Kuaiji, we can still seize the lands north of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎韓范亦上疏曰：「今晉室衰亂，江、淮南北，戶口無幾，戎馬單弱。

translations.literal: Han Fan, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Writers, also submitted a memorial, saying: "Now the house of Jin is in decline and disorder; north and south of the Yangtze and Huai the registered population is few and the war-horses few and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Palace writer attendant Han Fan also submitted a memorial: "The Jin house is in decline; north and south of the Yangtze and Huai there are few households and scant military strength.

sentences.zh: 重以桓玄悖逆，上下離心；

translations.literal: Moreover Huan Xuan is perverse and rebellious, and above and below are at odds in heart;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Huan Xuan is treasonous and the court is divided;

sentences.zh: 以陛下神武，發步騎一萬臨之，彼必土崩瓦解，兵不留行矣。

translations.literal: with Your Majesty's divine martial prowess, if you send ten thousand foot and horse against them, they will surely crumble like earth and dissolve like ice—your army will not pause in its march.
translations.idiomatic: with Your Majesty's martial prowess, a force of ten thousand infantry and cavalry will find them collapsing at once—your army will sweep through without pausing.

sentences.zh: 得而有之，秦、魏不足敵也。

translations.literal: Once you take it, Qin and Wei will not be worth opposing.
translations.idiomatic: Once we hold it, neither Later Qin nor Northern Wei will be a match for us.

sentences.zh: 拓地定功，正在今日。

translations.literal: To extend territory and fix merit—this is the very day.
translations.idiomatic: The moment to expand our domain and secure lasting glory is now.

sentences.zh: 失時不取，彼之豪傑誅滅桓玄，更修德政，豈惟建康不可得，江北亦無望矣。」

translations.literal: If you miss the time and do not take it, when their heroes have executed Huan Xuan and again cultivated virtuous government, not only will Jiankang be unobtainable—even the lands north of the river will be beyond hope."
translations.idiomatic: If we miss this chance, Jin heroes will destroy Huan Xuan and restore good government—and not only will Jiankang be beyond our reach, so will the entire north bank of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 備德曰：「朕以舊邦覆沒，欲先定中原，乃平蕩荊、揚，故未南征耳。

translations.literal: Murong De said: "I, because our old state was overthrown, wish first to settle the Central Plains and only then pacify Jing and Yang—therefore I have not campaigned south.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De replied, "Our old homeland was lost; I mean first to secure the Central Plains and only then pacify Jing and Yang—that is why I have not marched south.

sentences.zh: 其駐公卿議之。」

translations.literal: Let the ministers halt and deliberate on it."
translations.idiomatic: Let the ministers debate the matter."

sentences.zh: 因講武城西，步卒三十七萬人，騎五萬三千匹，車萬七千乘。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reviewed troops west of the city: three hundred seventy thousand foot soldiers, fifty-three thousand horses, and seventeen thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a grand military review west of the city: three hundred seventy thousand infantry, fifty-three thousand cavalry, and seventeen thousand chariots.

sentences.zh: 公卿皆以為玄新得志，未可圖，乃止。。

translations.literal: The ministers all held that Xuan had newly gained his ambition and could not yet be targeted, and so they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all judged that Huan Xuan had only just consolidated his power and was not yet vulnerable, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，楚王玄上表請歸籓，使帝作手詔固留之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, the King of Chu, Xuan, submitted a memorial requesting to return to his fief; he had the emperor compose a handwritten edict firmly detaining him.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, King of Chu Huan Xuan memorialized asking to return to his fief; he had the emperor issue a handwritten edict insisting that he remain.

sentences.zh: 又詐言錢塘臨平湖開，江州甘露降，使百僚集賀，用為己受命之符。

translations.literal: He also falsely reported that the Linping Lake at Qiantang had opened and that sweet dew had fallen in Jiang Province; he had the hundred officials assemble to congratulate him, using these as signs of his receiving the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: He also fabricated reports that Linping Lake at Qiantang had burst open and that sweet dew had fallen in Jiang Province, then assembled the officials to celebrate these as omens of his heavenly mandate.

sentences.zh: 又以前世皆有隱士，恥於己時獨無，求得西朝隱士安定皇甫謐六世孫希之，給其資用，使隱居山林；

translations.literal: Moreover, since former ages all had recluses, he was ashamed that in his time alone there were none; he sought out Xi Zhi, sixth-generation descendant of the Western Jin recluse Huangfu Mi of Anding, supplied his expenses, and had him dwell in seclusion in the mountains;
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that no recluses graced his reign when every past dynasty had them, he found Xi Zhi, sixth-generation descendant of the Jin recluse Huangfu Mi of Anding, funded his living, and installed him in mountain seclusion;

sentences.zh: 征為著作郎，使希之固辭不就，然後下詔旌禮，號曰高士。

translations.literal: he summoned him as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, had Xi Zhi firmly decline and not accept, and only then issued an edict honoring him, styling him Lofty Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: summoned him as gentleman of the Masters of Writing, had Xi Zhi firmly decline the post, and then issued an edict honoring him as a "Lofty Gentleman."

sentences.zh: 時人謂之「充隱。」

translations.literal: People of the time called him a "stock recluse."
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mocked him as a "staged recluse."

sentences.zh: 又欲廢錢用谷、帛及復肉刑，製作紛紜，志無一定，變更回復，卒無所施行。

translations.literal: He also wished to abolish coin and use grain and silk instead, and to restore corporal punishment; regulations proliferated, his intent was never fixed, and changes were reversed—in the end nothing was put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed abolishing coinage in favor of grain and silk and restoring corporal punishment; regulations piled up in confusion, his policies shifted constantly, and in the end nothing was enacted.

sentences.zh: 性復貪鄙，人士有法書、好畫及佳園宅，必假蒲博而取之；

translations.literal: By nature he was also greedy and base; if gentlemen had fine calligraphy, good paintings, or excellent gardens and houses, he was sure to take them through gambling on mat games;
translations.idiomatic: He was greedy and base by nature; whenever a gentleman owned fine calligraphy, good paintings, or an excellent estate, he would win them through rigged gambling;

sentences.zh: 尤愛珠玉，未嘗離手。。

translations.literal: he especially loved pearls and jade and never let them leave his hands.
translations.idiomatic: he was especially fond of pearls and jade and never let them out of his grasp.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，魏主珪立其子嗣為齊王，加位相國；

translations.literal: On the day yimao, the lord of Wei, Gui, made his son Si Prince of Qi and added the rank Chancellor of State;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day, Tuoba Gui made his son Si prince of Qi and appointed him chancellor of state;

sentences.zh: 紹為清河王，加征南大將軍；

translations.literal: Shao Prince of Qinghe, adding the rank General Who Campaigns South;
translations.idiomatic: Shao prince of Qinghe, with the added title general who campaigns south;

sentences.zh: 熙為陽平王；

translations.literal: Xi Prince of Yangping;
translations.idiomatic: Xi prince of Yangping;

sentences.zh: 曜為河南王。。

translations.literal: Yao Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: and Yao prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，魏將軍伊謂帥騎二萬襲高車餘種袁紇、烏頻；

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, the Wei general Yi Wei led twenty thousand horse in a surprise attack on the remnant Gaoche tribes Yuan He and Wu Pin;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day, Wei general Yi Wei led twenty thousand cavalry in a surprise attack on the remnant Gaoche tribes Yuan He and Wu Pin;

sentences.zh: 十一月，庚午，大破之。。

translations.literal: in the eleventh month, on the day gengwu, he routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: in the eleventh month, on gengwu day, he routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 詔楚王玄行天子禮樂，妃為王后，世子為太子。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the King of Chu, Xuan, to use the ritual and music of the Son of Heaven; his consort was made queen and his heir apparent crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: An edict authorized King of Chu Huan Xuan to use imperial ritual and music; his consort was made empress and his heir crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，卞范之為禪詔，使臨川王寶逼帝書之。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, Bian Fanzhi drafted the abdication edict and had the Prince of Linchuan, Bao, compel the emperor to write it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, Bian Fanzhi drafted the abdication edict and had Prince of Linchuan Sima Bao force the emperor to copy it out in his own hand.

sentences.zh: 寶，晞之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Bao was the great-grandson of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Bao was a great-grandson of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝臨軒，遣兼太保、領司徒王謐奉璽綬，禪位於楚。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the emperor faced the hall; he dispatched the concurrent Grand Mentor and concurrent Minister of Education Wang Mi to present the seal and cord and yield the throne to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day, the emperor took the throne hall and dispatched concurrent grand mentor and minister of education Wang Mi to present the imperial seal and cord and abdicate in favor of Chu.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝出居永安宮。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, the emperor moved out to dwell at the Yong'an Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day, the emperor moved to the Yong'an Palace.

sentences.zh: 癸未，遷太慶神主於琅邪國，穆章何皇后及琅邪王德文皆徙居司徒府。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei, the spirit tablets of the Grand Ancestor were moved to Langye State; Empress He of Mu and Zhang and the Prince of Langye, Dewen, were all relocated to the Minister of Education's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day, the imperial ancestral tablets were moved to Langye; Empress He and Prince of Langye Sima Dewen were relocated to the minister of education's residence.

sentences.zh: 百官詣姑孰勸進。

translations.literal: The hundred officials went to Gudu to urge his advance.
translations.idiomatic: The officials went to Gudu to urge Huan Xuan to accept the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚寅朔，玄築壇於九井山北，壬辰，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the cycle gengyin, Xuan built an altar north of Mount Jiujing; on renchen he ascended the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month (gengyin), Huan Xuan built an altar north of Mount Jiujing; on renchen day he ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 冊文多非溥晉室，或諫之，玄曰：「揖讓之文，正可陳之於下民耳，豈可欺上帝乎！」

translations.literal: The investiture text largely disparaged the house of Jin; when someone remonstrated, Xuan said: "The text of yielding the throne may be presented to the lower people—but how can one deceive the Supreme Lord!"
translations.idiomatic: The investiture text harshly denounced the Jin house; when someone objected, Huan Xuan said, "Abdication rhetoric is for the common people—how could I deceive Heaven itself!"

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元永始。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Yongshi.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 以南康之平固縣封帝為平固王，降何後為零陵縣君，琅邪王德文為石陽縣公，武陵王遵為彭澤縣候。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed the emperor as King of Pinggu with Pinggu County of Nankang; he reduced Empress He to Lady of Lingling County, the Prince of Langye Dewen to Duke of Shiyang County, and the Prince of Wuling Zun to Marquis of Pengze County.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed the former emperor as King of Pinggu at Pinggu County in Nankang; demoted Empress He to lady of Lingling County, Prince of Langye Sima Dewen to duke of Shiyang County, and Prince of Wuling Sima Zun to marquis of Pengze County.

sentences.zh: 追尊文溫為宣武皇帝，廟號太祖，南康公主為宣皇后，封子昇為豫章王。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Wen as Emperor Xuanwu, with temple name Taizu; the Princess of Nankang as Empress Xuan; and enfeoffed Zisheng as King of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Huan Wen as Emperor Xuanwu with temple name Taizu, Huan Wen's consort as Empress Xuan, and enfeoffed his son Zisheng as King of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 以會稽內史王愉為尚書僕射，愉子相國左長史綏為中書令。

translations.literal: He made Wang Yu, Administrator of Kuaiji, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Yu's son Sui, Left Chief Clerk of the Chancellor of State, Palace Writer-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Wang Yu, administrator of Kuaiji, vice director of the Masters of Writing, and Yu's son Sui, left chief clerk of the chancellor of state, palace writer-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 綏，桓氏之甥也。

translations.literal: Sui was a nephew of the Huan clan on his mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui was a nephew of the Huan clan by marriage.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，玄入建康宮，登御坐，而床忽陷，群下失色。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Xuan entered the Jiankang palace, ascended the imperial seat, and the couch suddenly sank; the assembled officials turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day, Huan Xuan entered the Jiankang palace and took the throne; the couch suddenly collapsed beneath him and the assembled officials turned pale.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文曰：「將由聖德深厚，地不能載。」

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen said: "It must be because the sage virtue is so deep and thick that the earth cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen said, "Your sacred virtue is so profound that even the earth cannot bear your weight."

sentences.zh: 玄大悅。

translations.literal: Xuan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 梁王珍之男臣孔樸奉珍之奔壽陽。

translations.literal: Kong Pu, a male attendant of the Prince of Liang, Zhenzhi, escorted Zhenzhi in flight to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Pu, a retainer of Prince of Liang Sima Zhenzhi, escorted him in flight to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 珍之，晞之曾孫也。。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi was the great-grandson of Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhenzhi was a great-grandson of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，燕王熙尊燕主垂之貴嬪段氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, the Yan king Murong Xi honored the honored consort of the Yan lord Chui, Lady Duan, as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day, Murong Xi of Northern Yan honored the honored consort of his predecessor Murong Chui, Lady Duan, as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 段氏，熙之慈母也。

translations.literal: Lady Duan was Xi's loving mother.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan was Murong Xi's foster mother.

sentences.zh: 己酉，立苻貴嬪為皇后，大赦。。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, he established the honored consort Fu as empress and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day, he made honored consort Fu empress and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，桓玄遷帝於尋陽。。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Huan Xuan moved the emperor to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day, Huan Xuan relocated the former emperor to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 燕以衛尉悅真為青州刺史，鎮新城；

translations.literal: Yan made Yue Zhen, Commandant of the Guards, Inspector of Qing Province, garrisoning Xincheng;
translations.idiomatic: Northern Yan appointed commandant of the guards Yue Zhen regional inspector of Qing Province, garrisoning Xincheng;

sentences.zh: 光大夫衛駒為并州刺史，鎮凡城。。

translations.literal: and the Grandee Physician Wei Ju Inspector of Bing Province, garrisoning Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: and grandee physician Wei Ju regional inspector of Bing Province, garrisoning Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，納桓溫神主於太廟。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Huan Wen's spirit tablet was installed in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day, Huan Wen's spirit tablet was installed in the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 桓玄臨聽訟觀閱囚徒，罪無輕重，多得原放；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan personally attended the hall of litigation to review prisoners; regardless of whether the crime was light or heavy, many were pardoned and released;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan personally reviewed prisoners in court; regardless of the severity of the offense, many were pardoned;

sentences.zh: 有干輿乞者，時或恤之。

translations.literal: if there were beggars who blocked his carriage, he would sometimes show them compassion.
translations.idiomatic: beggars who blocked his carriage were sometimes given alms.

sentences.zh: 其好行小惠如此。。

translations.literal: Such was his fondness for dispensing petty favors.
translations.idiomatic: Such were his petty displays of benevolence.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏主珪始命有司制冠服，以品秩為差。

translations.literal: This year, the lord of Wei, Gui, first ordered the relevant offices to devise caps and robes differentiated by rank and grade.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Tuoba Gui first ordered officials to devise caps and robes graded by rank.

sentences.zh: 然法度草創，多不稽古。。

translations.literal: Yet the regulations were newly drafted and largely did not follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: But the regulations were hastily drafted and largely ignored ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 安皇帝戊元興三年（甲辰，公元四零四年） 。

translations.literal: Emperor An, in the third year of Yuanxing of the wu cycle (jiachen, AD 404).
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An of Jin, third year of Yuanxing (jiachen, AD 404).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，桓玄立其妻劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, Huan Xuan established his wife, the Lady Liu, as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, Huan Xuan made his wife Lady Liu empress.

sentences.zh: 劉氏，喬之曾孫也。

translations.literal: The Lady Liu was the great-granddaughter of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu was a great-granddaughter of Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 玄以其祖彝以上名位不顯，不復追尊立廟。

translations.literal: Xuan, because the names and ranks of his ancestors from Yi upward were not illustrious, did not again pursue posthumous honors or establish temples.
translations.idiomatic: Because his ancestors from Huan Yi upward had held no distinguished titles, Huan Xuan declined to establish ancestral temples for them.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍徐廣曰：「敬其父則子悅，請依故事立七廟。」

translations.literal: Xu Guang, Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, said: "When one honors his father, the son is pleased—please follow precedent and establish the seven temples."
translations.idiomatic: Regular attendant Xu Guang said, "Honoring one's father brings joy to the son—I urge you to establish the seven ancestral temples as precedent requires."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「禮，太祖東向，左昭右穆。

translations.literal: Xuan said: "By ritual, the Grand Ancestor faces east, with Zhao on the left and Mu on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan replied, "By ritual law, the founding ancestor faces east, with zhao on the left and mu on the right.

sentences.zh: 晉立七廟，宣帝不得正東向之位，何足法也！」

translations.literal: When Jin established the seven temples, the Emperor Xuan could not occupy the due-east position—what is there worth taking as model!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jin established its seven temples, even Emperor Xuan could not face due east—what is there worth imitating!"

sentences.zh: 秘書監卞承之謂廣曰：「若宗廟之祭果不及祖，有以知楚德之不長矣。」

translations.literal: Bian Chengzhi, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, said to Guang: "If the ancestral temple sacrifices truly do not reach the ancestors, one may know that the virtue of Chu will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Bian Chengzhi told Xu Guang privately, "If the ancestral sacrifices do not reach back to his forebears, we may know that the Chu dynasty will not endure long."

sentences.zh: 廣，邈之弟也。。

translations.literal: Guang was the younger brother of Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang was a younger brother of Xu Miao.

sentences.zh: 玄自即位，心常不自安。

translations.literal: From the time Xuan ascended the throne, his heart was never at ease.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he took the throne, Huan Xuan was never at ease in his own mind.

sentences.zh: 二月，己丑朔，夜，濤水入石頭，流殺人甚多，歡嘩震天。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day of the cycle jichou, at night the tidal bore entered Shitou, the current killing many people; shouts and clamor shook heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first night of the month (jichou), a tidal bore surged into Shitou and drowned many people; the uproar shook the heavens.

sentences.zh: 玄聞之，懼，曰：「奴輩作矣！」。

translations.literal: When Xuan heard of it, he was afraid and said: "The slave lot are acting!"
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan heard of it, he was frightened and cried, "The slaves are rising!"

sentences.zh: 玄性苛細，好自矜伐。

translations.literal: Xuan was by nature harsh and minute, fond of praising his own merits.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was petty and harsh by nature, and fond of boasting of his own achievements.

sentences.zh: 主者奏事，或一字不體，或片辭之謬，必加糾擿，以示聰明。

translations.literal: When officials presented business, if a single character was not in proper form or a phrase was in error, he was sure to correct and expose it, to display his intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: When officials submitted memorials, he would seize on a single miswritten character or a flawed phrase and publicly rebuke the author to display his own sharpness.

sentences.zh: 尚書答詔誤書「春蒐為「春菟」，自左丞王納之以下，凡所關署，皆被降黜。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing, in replying to an edict, mistakenly wrote "spring hunt" as "spring hare"; from the Left Vice Director Wang Nazhi downward, all who had affixed their seals were demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing, drafting a reply to an edict, wrote "spring hare" for "spring hunt"; from left vice director Wang Nazhi downward, every official who had countersigned the document was demoted or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 或手注直官，或自用令史，詔令紛紜，有司奉答不暇，而紀綱不治，奏案停積，不能知也。

translations.literal: Sometimes he personally annotated the direct officials, or himself used clerks; edicts and commands proliferated in confusion, the relevant offices could not keep up with replies, yet the framework of governance was not ordered, memorials piled up unprocessed, and he could not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes annotated documents himself or drafted orders through personal clerks; edicts piled up in confusion, offices could not keep pace with replies, governance fell into disorder, and memorials stacked up unread while he remained unaware.

sentences.zh: 又性好游畋，或一日數出。

translations.literal: Moreover he was fond of roaming and hunting and might go out several times in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He was also fond of hunting and might go out several times in a single day.

sentences.zh: 遷居東宮，更繕宮室，土木並興，督迫嚴促，朝野騷然，思亂者眾。。

translations.literal: He moved to the Eastern Palace and again repaired the palace buildings; earthworks and timber construction rose together, supervision was harsh and urgent, court and countryside were in turmoil, and many thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He moved into the Eastern Palace and launched vast construction projects; labor was driven relentlessly, the court and countryside were in turmoil, and many began to think of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 玄遣使加益州刺史毛璩散騎常侍、左將軍。

translations.literal: Xuan sent envoys to add to Mao Jin, Inspector of Yi Province, the ranks Regular Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan sent envoys to promote regional inspector Mao Jin of Yi Province to regular attendant within the yellow gates and general of the left.

sentences.zh: 璩執留玄使，不受其命。

translations.literal: Jin detained Xuan's envoys and did not accept the command.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin detained Huan Xuan's envoys and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 璩，寶之孫也。

translations.literal: Jin was the grandson of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin was a grandson of Mao Bao.

sentences.zh: 玄以桓希為梁州刺史，分命諸將戍三巴以備之。

translations.literal: Xuan made Huan Xi Inspector of Liang Province and separately ordered various generals to garrison the Three Ba to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan appointed Huan Xi regional inspector of Liang Province and stationed generals in the Three Ba region to guard against Mao Jin.

sentences.zh: 璩傳檄遠近，列玄罪狀，遣巴東太守柳約之、建平太守羅述、征虜司馬甄季之擊破希等，仍帥眾進屯白帝。。

translations.literal: Jin circulated a proclamation far and near listing Xuan's crimes; he sent the Administrator of Badong Liu Yuezhi, the Administrator of Jianping Luo Shu, and the Campaigning General's Chief of Staff Zhen Jizhi to attack and defeat Xi and the others, then led his host forward to encamp at Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin issued a proclamation throughout the region listing Huan Xuan's crimes, sent administrators Liu Yuezhi of Badong, Luo Shu of Jianping, and campaigning general's chief of staff Zhen Jizhi to defeat Huan Xi and his forces, then advanced to encamp at Baidi.

sentences.zh: 劉裕從徐、兗二州刺史，安成王桓修入朝。

translations.literal: Liu Yu followed the Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces, the Prince of Ancheng, Huan Xiu, in entering the court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu accompanied Huan Xiu, regional inspector of Xu and Yan provinces and Prince of Ancheng, to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄謂王謐曰：「裕風骨不常，蓋人傑也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said to Wang Mi, "Yu has an uncommon bearing and manner; he is surely a hero among men."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan said to Wang Mi, "Liu Yu's presence is unlike that of ordinary men—he is clearly a hero of the age."

sentences.zh: 每游集，必引接殷勤，贈賜甚厚。

translations.literal: At every gathering for pleasure he would draw him near with eager courtesy and bestow gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: At every social gathering he drew Liu Yu close with warm attention and lavished generous gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 玄後劉氏，有智鑒，謂玄曰：「劉裕龍行虎步，視瞻不凡，恐終不為人下，不如早除之。」

translations.literal: Xuan's consort, the Lady Liu, had insight and judgment; she said to Xuan, "Liu Yu moves like a dragon and strides like a tiger; his gaze is extraordinary—I fear he will never remain beneath others. Better to eliminate him early."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's wife Lady Liu was shrewd and perceptive. She told him, "Liu Yu walks with a dragon's grace and a tiger's power, and his bearing is unmistakable. I fear he will never serve under anyone. You should kill him while you still can."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「我方平蕩中原，非裕莫可用者；

translations.literal: Xuan said, "I am just now pacifying the Central Plain; there is no one I can employ except Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan replied, "I am in the midst of pacifying the Central Plains. Liu Yu is indispensable—no one else will do;

sentences.zh: 俟關、河平定，然後別議之耳。」。

translations.literal: when the passes of Hangu and the Yellow River are pacified, then we may discuss it separately—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: once the Guan region and the Yellow River are secured, we can decide what to do with him."

sentences.zh: 玄以桓弘為青州刺史，鎮廣陵；

translations.literal: Xuan made Huan Hong regional inspector of Qing Province and stationed him at Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan appointed Huan Hong regional inspector of Qing Province, with his headquarters at Guangling;

sentences.zh: 刁逵為豫州刺史，鎮歷陽。

translations.literal: Diao Kui was made regional inspector of Yu Province and stationed at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: and Diao Kui regional inspector of Yu Province, stationed at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 弘，修之弟；

translations.literal: Hong was Xiu's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Hong was the younger brother of Huan Xiu;

sentences.zh: 逵，彝之子也。。

translations.literal: Kui was Yi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Kui was the son of Diao Yi.

sentences.zh: 劉裕與何無忌同舟還京口，密謀興復晉室。

translations.literal: Liu Yu and He Wuji returned to Jingkou in the same boat, secretly plotting to restore the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu and He Wuji sailed back to Jingkou together and secretly plotted to restore the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 劉邁弟毅家於京口，亦與無忌謀討玄。

translations.literal: Liu Mai's younger brother Yi had his home at Jingkou, and also with Wuji plotted to attack Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi's family lived at Jingkou—he was the younger brother of Liu Mai—and he joined He Wuji in planning a rising against Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「桓氏強盛，其可圖乎？」

translations.literal: Wuji said, "The Huan clan is powerful—can they be targeted?"
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji asked, "The Huan clan is at the height of its power. Can we really hope to overthrow them?"

sentences.zh: 毅曰：「天下自有強弱，苟為失道，雖強易弱，正患事主難得耳。」

translations.literal: Yi said, "Under Heaven there is always strength and weakness; if one loses the Way, though strong one easily becomes weak—the only worry is finding a worthy leader."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi answered, "Power under Heaven rises and falls. When a regime loses the Mandate, the mighty fall swiftly. Our real problem is finding a leader worth following."

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「天下草澤之中非無英雄也。」

translations.literal: Wuji said, "Among the common folk of the realm heroes are not lacking."
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji said, "Heroes are not hard to find among the common people of the realm."

sentences.zh: 毅曰：「所見唯有劉下邳。」

translations.literal: Yi said, "Of those I have seen, only Liu of Xiapi."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi said, "Of all I have met, only Liu Yu of Xiapi."

sentences.zh: 無忌笑而不答，還以告裕，遂與毅定謀。。

translations.literal: Wuji smiled and did not answer; returning he told Yu, and thus with Yi fixed the plot.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji smiled and said nothing, but when he reported the conversation to Liu Yu, Yu and Liu Yi forged their alliance.

sentences.zh: 初，太原王元德及弟仲德為苻氏起兵攻燕主垂，不克，來奔，朝廷以元德為弘農太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Yuande of Taiyuan and his younger brother Zhongde had raised troops for the Fu clan to attack the Yan ruler Chui, failed, and came as refugees; the court made Yuande administrator of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wang Yuande of Taiyuan and his brother Wang Zhongde had raised troops on behalf of Former Qin to attack Murong Chui of Later Yan. When they failed, they fled south and were given refuge; the court appointed Wang Yuande administrator of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 仲德見桓玄稱帝，謂人曰：「自古革命誠非一族，然今之起者恐不足以成大事。」。

translations.literal: Zhongde saw Huan Xuan declare himself emperor and said to people, "Since antiquity dynastic change has indeed not been confined to one clan, but those rising now—I fear they are not enough to accomplish a great affair."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhongde saw Huan Xuan declare himself emperor, he remarked, "Dynasties have always changed hands, but I doubt this usurper has what it takes to build anything lasting."

sentences.zh: 平昌孟昶為青州主簿，桓弘使昶至建康，玄見而悅之，謂劉邁曰：「素士中得一尚書郎，卿與其州裡，寧相識否？」

translations.literal: Meng Chang of Pingchang was chief clerk of Qing Province; Huan Hong sent Chang to Jiankang; Xuan saw him and was pleased, saying to Liu Mai, "Among plain scholars I have found one fit for an Attendant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing—you are from the same district; do you perhaps know him?"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang of Pingchang served as chief clerk in Qing Province. When Huan Hong sent him to Jiankang, Huan Xuan took a liking to him and asked Liu Mai, "I've found a plain scholar worthy of an appointment in the Masters of Writing. He comes from your province—do you know him?"

sentences.zh: 邁素與昶不善，對曰：「臣在京口，不聞昶有異能，唯聞父子紛紛更相贈詩耳。」

translations.literal: Mai had long been on bad terms with Chang and replied, "When I was at Jingkou I never heard that Chang had unusual ability—only that father and son busily exchanged poems with each other."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mai had never liked Meng Chang. He replied, "When I was at Jingkou I heard nothing of any special talent in him—only that he and his father kept sending each other poems."

sentences.zh: 玄笑而止，。

translations.literal: Xuan laughed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan laughed and dropped the subject.

sentences.zh: 昶聞而恨之，既還京口，裕謂昶曰：「草間當有英雄起，卿頗聞乎？」

translations.literal: Chang heard and resented it; having returned to Jingkou, Yu said to Chang, "Among the grass roots heroes ought to rise—have you heard of any?"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang nursed a grudge. Back in Jingkou, Liu Yu asked him, "Surely heroes are stirring among the common folk. Have you heard of any?"

sentences.zh: 昶曰：「今日英雄有誰，正當是卿耳！」。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Who is the hero of today? It can only be you!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang answered, "Who is the hero of our day? You, sir—that is who!"

sentences.zh: 於是裕、毅、無忌、元德、仲德、昶及裕弟道規、任城魏詠之、高平檀憑之、琅邪諸葛長民、河內太守隨西辛扈興、振威將軍東莞童厚之，相與合謀起兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu, Yi, Wuji, Yuande, Zhongde, Chang, and Yu's younger brother Daogui, Wei Yongzhi of Rencheng, Tan Pingzhi of Gaoping, Zhuge Changmin of Langye, Xin Huxing of Suixi, administrator of Henei, and Tong Houzhi of Dongguan, General Who Rouses Might—all together joined in plotting to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liu Yu, Liu Yi, He Wuji, Wang Yuande, Wang Zhongde, Meng Chang, Liu Yu's brother Liu Daogui, Wei Yongzhi of Rencheng, Tan Pingzhi of Gaoping, Zhuge Changmin of Langye, Xin Huxing of Suixi (administrator of Henei), and Tong Houzhi of Dongguan (General Who Rouses Might) joined forces to plot a rising.

sentences.zh: 道規為桓弘中兵參軍，裕使毅就道規及昶於江北，共殺弘，據廣陵；

translations.literal: Daogui was middle army adjutant under Huan Hong; Yu sent Yi to join Daogui and Chang north of the river, together to kill Hong and hold Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daogui served as middle army adjutant on Huan Hong's staff. Liu Yu sent Liu Yi north of the Yangtze to join Daogui and Meng Chang in killing Huan Hong and seizing Guangling;

sentences.zh: 長民為刁逵參軍，使長民殺逵，據歷陽；

translations.literal: Changmin was adjutant to Diao Kui; he was to have Changmin kill Kui and hold Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin was on Diao Kui's staff; he was to kill Kui and hold Liyang;

sentences.zh: 元德、扈興、厚之在建康，使之聚眾攻玄為內應；

translations.literal: Yuande, Huxing, and Houzhi were in Jiankang, to have them gather crowds and attack Xuan as inner response;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuande, Xin Huxing, and Tong Houzhi were to remain in Jiankang, gather supporters, and strike Huan Xuan from within;

sentences.zh: 刻期齊發。。

translations.literal: A date was fixed for simultaneous rising.
translations.idiomatic: They set a date for coordinated action on all fronts.

sentences.zh: 孟昶妻周氏富於財，昶謂之曰：「劉邁毀我於桓公，使我一生滄陷，我決當作賊。

translations.literal: Meng Chang's wife, the Lady Zhou, was rich in wealth; Chang said to her, "Liu Mai slandered me before Duke Huan, causing my whole life to sink into ruin—I am resolved to become a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang's wife Lady Zhou was wealthy. He told her, "Liu Mai defamed me to Duke Huan and ruined my career. I am going to rebel.

sentences.zh: 卿幸早離絕，脫得富貴，相迎不晚也。」

translations.literal: You had best sever ties early; if I attain wealth and honor, welcoming you back will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: You should leave me now. If I succeed, I will send for you—it won't be too late."

sentences.zh: 周我曰：「君父母在堂，欲建非常之謀，豈婦人所能諫！

translations.literal: Lady Zhou said, "Your parents are still alive in their hall; you wish to undertake an extraordinary plot—how could a woman dissuade you!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou replied, "Your parents are still alive. You are planning something momentous—what woman could talk you out of it?

sentences.zh: 事之不成，當於奚官中奉養大家，義無歸志也。」

translations.literal: If the affair does not succeed, I shall in the eunuch bureau support the greater family—righteousness admits no thought of returning home."
translations.idiomatic: If you fail, I will enter palace service and support your family. I will not abandon you."

sentences.zh: 昶悵然久之而起。

translations.literal: Chang was despondent a long time, then rose.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang sat in silence for a long time, then rose.

sentences.zh: 周氏追昶坐，曰：「觀君舉措，非謀及婦人者，不過欲得財物耳。」

translations.literal: Lady Zhou pursued Chang and made him sit, saying, "Observing your conduct, this is not a plot a woman need share—you only want property, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou pulled him back down and said, "Judging by your manner, this isn't some woman's business—you only want my money."

sentences.zh: 因指懷中兒示之曰：「此兒可賣，亦當不惜。」

translations.literal: She then pointed to the child in her bosom and showed him, saying, "This child may be sold—I would not spare him either."
translations.idiomatic: She pointed to the infant in her arms and said, "You may sell this child too. I would not hesitate."

sentences.zh: 遂傾貲以給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon she poured out her wealth to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: She emptied her coffers to fund the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 昶弟顗妻，周氏之從妹也，周氏紿之曰：「昨夜夢殊不祥，門內絳色物宜悉取以為厭勝。」

translations.literal: The wife of Chang's younger brother Yi was Lady Zhou's cousin on the mother's side; Lady Zhou deceived her, saying, "Last night I dreamed something very inauspicious—all crimson things within the gate should be taken to make averting charms."
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Meng Chang's younger brother Meng Yi was Lady Zhou's cousin. Lady Zhou tricked her, saying, "I had a terrible dream last night. You should gather every piece of red cloth in the house for a protective rite."

sentences.zh: 妹信而與之，遂盡縫以為軍士袍。。

translations.literal: The cousin believed and gave them to her; thereupon she sewed them all into soldiers' robes.
translations.idiomatic: The cousin believed her and handed over the cloth. Lady Zhou had it all sewn into uniforms for the troops.

sentences.zh: 何無忌夜於屏風裡草檄文，其母，劉牢之姊也，登榆密窺之，泣曰：「吾不及東海呂母明矣。

translations.literal: He Wuji by night behind a screen drafted a proclamation; his mother, Liu Laozhi's elder sister, climbed the elm and secretly peered, weeping, "I am not as clear-sighted as the Lady Lü of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: One night He Wuji drafted a proclamation behind a screen. His mother—elder sister of Liu Laozhi—climbed onto the elm outside and watched through a crack. She wept and said, "I am not the equal of Lady Lü of Donghai in foresight.

sentences.zh: 汝能如此，吾復何恨！」

translations.literal: You can do thus—what regret have I again!"
translations.idiomatic: If you can do this, I have nothing left to regret!"

sentences.zh: 問所與同謀者，曰：「劉裕。」

translations.literal: She asked with whom he plotted together; he said, "Liu Yu."
translations.idiomatic: She asked who his co-conspirators were. He answered, "Liu Yu."

sentences.zh: 母尤喜，因為言玄必敗，舉事必成之理以勸之。。

translations.literal: The mother was especially pleased, and thereupon set forth the reasoning why Xuan was sure to be defeated and the rising was sure to succeed, to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was overjoyed and urged him on with reasons why Huan Xuan was doomed to fall and why their enterprise was bound to succeed.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，裕托以遊獵，與無忌收合徒眾，得百餘人。

translations.literal: On yimao, Yu using hunting as pretext, with Wuji gathered adherents, obtaining a hundred-odd men.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day, Liu Yu used a hunting expedition as cover to gather followers with He Wuji, mustering a little over a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詰旦，京口城開，無忌著傳詔服，稱敕使，居前，徒眾隨之齊入，即斬桓修以徇。

translations.literal: On bingchen, at dawn, Jingkou's gates opened; Wuji wore imperial messenger garb, declaring himself an envoy with edict, went ahead, the crowd entered together, and immediately beheaded Huan Xiu as example.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on bingchen day the gates of Jingkou opened. He Wuji dressed as an imperial messenger, proclaimed himself a bearer of edicts, and led the column inside. The men poured in after him and immediately beheaded Huan Xiu as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 修司馬刁弘帥文武佐吏來赴，裕登城謂之曰：「郭江州已奉乘輿返正於尋陽，我等並被密詔，誅除逆黨，今日賊玄之首已當梟梟於大航矣。

translations.literal: Xiu's marshal Diao Hong led civil and military subordinates to come; Yu ascended the wall and said to them, "Regional Inspector Guo of Jiang has already brought the imperial carriage to restore legitimacy at Xunyang; we all have secret edicts to exterminate the rebel faction—today the rebel Xuan's head should already be displayed at Dahang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu's marshal Diao Hong marched up with the civil and military staff. Liu Yu mounted the wall and called out, "Governor Guo of Jiangzhou has already escorted the emperor back to legitimacy at Xunyang. We have all received secret edicts to wipe out the traitors. By now the rebel Huan Xuan's head should already be on display at the Great Ferry.

sentences.zh: 諸君非大晉之臣乎？

translations.literal: Are you gentlemen not ministers of Great Jin?
translations.idiomatic: Are you not servants of the Jin dynasty?

sentences.zh: 今來欲何為？」

translations.literal: Coming now, what do you intend?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you mean by coming here now?"

sentences.zh: 弘等信之，收眾而退。。

translations.literal: Hong and the others believed it and withdrew their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Hong and his men believed him and withdrew their troops.

sentences.zh: 裕問無忌曰：「今急須一府主簿，何由得之？」

translations.literal: Yu asked Wuji, "Now we urgently need a headquarters chief clerk—how can we obtain one?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu asked He Wuji, "We need a chief clerk for headquarters at once. Where can we find one?"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「無過劉道民。」

translations.literal: Wuji said, "None surpasses Liu Daomin."
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji said, "No one better than Liu Daomin."

sentences.zh: 道民者，東莞劉穆之也。

translations.literal: Daomin was Liu Muzhi of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daomin" was Liu Muzhi of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「吾亦識之。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "I too know him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu said, "I know him too."

sentences.zh: 即馳信召焉。

translations.literal: Immediately he sent a fast messenger to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent a messenger at full gallop to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 時穆之聞京口歡噪聲，晨起，出陌頭，屬與信會。

translations.literal: At the time Muzhi heard the clamor of rejoicing at Jingkou; rising early, he went out to the lane's end, and happened to meet the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi had heard the uproar of celebration in Jingkou. He rose early and stepped into the lane, where he ran straight into the messenger.

sentences.zh: 穆之直視不言者久之，既而返室，壞布裳為褲，往見裕。

translations.literal: Muzhi stared straight ahead and did not speak for a long time; then he returned to his room, tore his cloth robe to make trousers, and went to see Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi stared ahead in silence for a long moment, then went back inside, ripped his cloth robe into trousers, and went to see Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「始舉大義，方造艱難，須一軍吏甚急，卿謂誰堪其選？」

translations.literal: Yu said, "We have just raised the great cause and are entering hardship; we urgently need a military clerk—whom do you think is fit for the post?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu said, "We have just launched a great enterprise and hardship lies ahead. We need a military administrator at once. Who do you think is right for the job?"

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「貴府始建，軍吏實須其才，倉猝之際，略當無見逾者。」

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "Your headquarters is just established; the military clerk truly needs talent—for the moment, roughly speaking, none should be seen to surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi said, "Your command is newly formed and needs a man of real ability. At a moment like this, I doubt anyone could do better."

sentences.zh: 裕笑曰：「卿能自屈，吾事濟矣。」

translations.literal: Yu smiled and said, "You can humble yourself—my affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu smiled and said, "If you will take the post yourself, my cause is assured."

sentences.zh: 即於坐署主簿。。

translations.literal: Immediately at the seat he appointed him chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On the spot he appointed him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 孟昶勸桓弘其日出獵，天未明，開門出獵人；

translations.literal: Meng Chang urged Huan Hong to go hunting that day; before dawn the gates opened to let out hunters;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang persuaded Huan Hong to go hunting that day. Before dawn the gates opened to admit the hunting party;

sentences.zh: 昶與劉毅、劉道規帥壯士數十人直入，弘方啖粥，即斬之。

translations.literal: Chang with Liu Yi and Liu Daogui led several tens of stalwarts straight in; Hong was just eating porridge—they immediately beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang, Liu Yi, and Liu Daogui led several dozen stalwarts straight inside. Huan Hong was still at his morning porridge when they cut him down.

sentences.zh: 因收眾濟江。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered the forces and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: They then gathered their men and crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 裕使毅誅刁弘。。

translations.literal: Yu had Yi execute Diao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu had Liu Yi put Diao Hong to death.

sentences.zh: 先是，裕遣同謀周安穆入建康報劉邁，邁雖酬許，意甚惶懼。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu had sent fellow conspirator Zhou Anmu into Jiankang to inform Liu Mai; Mai though he answered in agreement, in mind was very fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Yu had sent his co-conspirator Zhou Anmu to Jiankang to alert Liu Mai. Mai agreed to cooperate but was terrified.

sentences.zh: 安穆慮事洩，乃馳歸。

translations.literal: Anmu feared the affair would leak and galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Zhou Anmu galloped back.

sentences.zh: 玄以為邁為竟陵太守，邁欲亟之郡。

translations.literal: Xuan made Mai administrator of Jingling; Mai wished to hurry to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had appointed Liu Mai administrator of Jingling, and Mai was eager to reach his post.

sentences.zh: 是夜，玄與邁書曰：「北府人情雲何？

translations.literal: That night Xuan wrote to Mai, "How stand the sentiments of the Northern Headquarters?
translations.idiomatic: That night Huan Xuan wrote to Liu Mai: "What is the mood among the Northern Headquarters troops?

sentences.zh: 卿近見劉裕何所道？」

translations.literal: What did Liu Yu say when you recently saw him?"
translations.idiomatic: What has Liu Yu been saying lately, in your recent dealings with him?"

sentences.zh: 邁謂玄已知其謀，晨起，白之。

translations.literal: Mai thought Xuan already knew their plot; rising early, he reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mai assumed Huan Xuan had discovered the plot. At dawn he went and confessed everything.

sentences.zh: 玄大驚，封邁為重安侯。

translations.literal: Xuan was greatly alarmed and enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was badly shaken and enfeoffed Liu Mai as Marquis of Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 既而嫌邁不執安穆，使得逃去，乃殺之，悉誅元德、扈興、厚之等。。

translations.literal: Presently resenting that Mai had not seized Anmu and let him escape, he killed Mai and executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and the rest entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he grew angry that Liu Mai had not arrested Zhou Anmu and had let him escape. He had Mai killed and put Wang Yuande, Xin Huxing, Tong Houzhi, and the other conspirators in Jiankang to death.

sentences.zh: 眾推劉裕為盟，總督徐州事，以孟昶為長史，守京口，檀憑之為司馬。

translations.literal: The multitude pushed Liu Yu as covenant leader, overall director of Xu Province affairs; made Meng Chang chief clerk, guarding Jingkou; Tan Pingzhi as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels acclaimed Liu Yu as their leader and gave him overall command of Xu Province. Meng Chang became his chief clerk and held Jingkou; Tan Pingzhi was made marshal.

sentences.zh: 彭城人應募者，裕悉使郡主簿劉鐘統之。

translations.literal: Those from Pengcheng who answered the call, Yu had the commandery chief clerk Liu Zhong command them all.
translations.idiomatic: Every recruit from Pengcheng was placed under the command of the commandery chief clerk Liu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，裕帥二州之眾千七百人，軍於竹裡，移檄遠近，聲言益州刺史毛璩已定荊楚，江州刺史郭昶之奉迎主上返正於尋陽，鎮北參軍王元德等並帥部曲保據石頭，揚武將軍諸葛長尼已據歷陽。。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Yu led the forces of two provinces, seventeen hundred men, encamped at Zhuli, and issued a proclamation far and near, proclaiming that Regional Inspector Mao Jin of Yi Province had already pacified Jing and Chu, Regional Inspector Guo Gongzhi of Jiang had welcomed the sovereign to restore legitimacy at Xunyang, Campaigning North Adjutant Wang Yuande and others had all led their retainers to hold Stone City, and General Who Displays Martial Might Zhuge Changmin had already held Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Liu Yu marched south with seventeen hundred men from two provinces and encamped at Zhuli. He sent proclamations far and wide claiming that Mao Jin, regional inspector of Yi Province, had pacified Jing and Chu; that Guo Gongzhi, regional inspector of Jiangzhou, was escorting the emperor back to legitimacy at Xunyang; that Wang Yuande and other northern staff officers were holding Stone City with their retainers; and that Zhuge Changmin, General Who Displays Martial Might, had already seized Liyang.

sentences.zh: 玄移還上宮，召侍官皆入止省中；

translations.literal: Xuan moved back to the Upper Palace and summoned all attendants to enter and remain within the inner offices;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan withdrew to the Upper Palace and ordered all palace attendants to remain inside the inner compound;

sentences.zh: 加揚州刺史新安王桓謙征討都督，以殷仲文代桓修為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: he added Prince Xin'an Huan Qian of Yang Province as campaign-pacification commander-in-chief, and made Yin Zhongwen replace Huan Xiu as regional inspector of Xu and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: he made Prince Xin'an Huan Qian of Yang Province supreme commander for the punitive campaign, and appointed Yin Zhongwen to replace Huan Xiu as regional inspector of Xu and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 謙等請亟遣兵擊裕，玄曰：「彼兵銳甚，計出萬死，若有蹉跌，則彼氣成而吾事去矣；

translations.literal: Qian and the others asked urgently to send troops to strike Yu; Xuan said, "Their troops are very sharp; they plan to stake everything on one throw—if there is any stumble, their morale will be made and our affair will be lost;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian and his officers urged an immediate attack on Liu Yu. Huan Xuan said, "Their troops are fierce and desperate. They are gambling everything on this move. One setback on our side will steel their morale and ruin us.

sentences.zh: 不如屯大眾於覆舟山以待之。

translations.literal: better to mass a great host on Mount Fushan and await them.
translations.idiomatic: Better to mass our main force on Mount Fushan and wait for them.

sentences.zh: 彼空行二百里，無所得，銳氣已挫，忽見大軍，必驚愕；
