translations.literal: They will march two hundred li in vain and gain nothing; their sharp spirit will already be blunted—suddenly seeing a great army, they are sure to be startled;
translations.idiomatic: They will march two hundred li and achieve nothing. Their edge will dull. When they suddenly see a great army, they will be stunned.

sentences.zh: 我按兵堅陣，勿與交鋒，彼求戰不得，自然散走，此策之上也。」

translations.literal: we hold our troops and firm our lines, do not cross blades with them—when they cannot obtain battle, naturally they will scatter and flee; this is the supreme stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: We hold our ground in a solid formation and refuse battle. Unable to fight, they will melt away of their own accord. That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 謙等固請擊之，乃遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衛將軍皇甫敷相繼北上。

translations.literal: Qian and the others firmly asked to strike them; thereupon he sent Administrator of Dunqiu Wu Fuzhi and General of the Right Guard Huangfu Fu in succession north.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian and the others pressed hard for an attack. Huan Xuan then sent Wu Fuzhi, administrator of Dunqiu, and Huangfu Fu, General of the Right Guard, north in succession.

sentences.zh: 玄憂懼特甚。

translations.literal: Xuan was anxious and fearful in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was consumed with fear.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「裕等烏合微弱，勢必無成，陛下何慮之深！」

translations.literal: Someone said, "Yu and the others are a rabble, weak—surely they cannot succeed; Your Majesty, why worry so deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Liu Yu and his band are a rabble—weak and bound to fail. Why does Your Majesty worry so much?"

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「劉裕足為一世之雄，劉毅家無擔石之儲，樗蒲一擲百萬，何無忌酷似其舅；

translations.literal: Xuan said, "Liu Yu is fully fit to be a hero of an age; Liu Yi's house has not a dan or shi of stores, yet at backgammon one throw is a million; He Wuji is the very image of his maternal uncle;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan said, "Liu Yu is a hero born once in an age. Liu Yi has not a bushel of grain at home, yet he will stake a million on a single throw at dice. He Wuji is the living image of his uncle Liu Laozhi.

sentences.zh: 共舉大事，何謂無成！」。

translations.literal: together they raise a great affair—how can one say they cannot succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: Together they have launched a great enterprise. How can you call that bound to fail?"

sentences.zh: 南涼王辱檀畏秦之強，乃去年號，罷尚書丞郎官，遣參軍關尚使於秦。

translations.literal: The King of Southern Liang, Rutan, feared Qin's strength; thereupon he removed his era name, abolished the posts of Masters of Writing registrars and attendants, and sent adjutant Guan Shang as envoy to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Rutan, king of Southern Liang, fearing the might of Former Qin, dropped his era name, abolished the secretariat registrar and attendant posts, and sent his adjutant Guan Shang as envoy to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦王興曰：「車騎獻款稱籓，而擅興兵造大城，豈為臣之道乎？」

translations.literal: The King of Qin, Xing, said, "The General of Chariots and Cavalry has offered sincerity and called himself a vassal, yet on his own authority he has raised troops and built a great city—how is this the way of a minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yao Xing of Later Qin said, "The Prince of Chariots and Cavalry has sworn fealty and called himself my vassal, yet he has mustered troops and raised a great fortress without leave. Is this how a subject should behave?"

sentences.zh: 尚曰：「王公設險以守其國，先王之制也。

translations.literal: Shang said, "Kings and dukes establish defenses to guard their states—this is the former kings' institution.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Shang replied, "For kings and princes to hold strategic barriers and defend their domains is the ancient royal law.

sentences.zh: 車騎僻在遐籓，密邇勍寇，蓋為國家重門之防，不圖陛下忽以為嫌。」

translations.literal: The General of Chariots and Cavalry dwells secluded in a distant border, close to a powerful enemy; he was making for the state a heavy-gate defense—he did not expect Your Majesty would suddenly regard it as suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: "The Prince holds a remote frontier post, pressed hard by a formidable foe. He was only strengthening the empire's outer gate. I never imagined Your Majesty would take this as grounds for suspicion."

sentences.zh: 興善之。

translations.literal: Xing approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with this explanation.

sentences.zh: 辱檀求領涼州，興不許。。

translations.literal: Rutan begged to take charge of Liangzhou; Xing did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tufa Rutan asked to be made governor of Liangzhou; Xing refused.

sentences.zh: 初，袁真殺朱憲，憲弟綽逃奔桓溫。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Yuan Zhen killed Zhu Xian; Xian's younger brother Chuo fled and rushed to Huan Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yuan Zhen had killed Zhu Xian. Xian's younger brother Chuo fled to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫克壽陽，綽輒發真棺，戮其屍。

translations.literal: Wen captured Shouyang; Chuo forthwith opened Zhen's coffin and mutilated his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took Shouyang, Chuo opened Yuan Zhen's coffin and defiled the body.

sentences.zh: 溫怒，將殺之，桓沖請而免之。

translations.literal: Wen was angry and was about to kill him; Huan Chong pleaded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was furious and meant to put him to death, but Huan Chong interceded and saved him.

sentences.zh: 綽事沖如父，沖薨，綽嘔血而卒。

translations.literal: Chuo served Chong as a father; when Chong died, Chuo vomited blood and expired.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo had served Chong as a son serves a father. When Chong died, Chuo coughed blood and died.

sentences.zh: 劉裕克京口，以綽子齡石為建武參軍。

translations.literal: Liu Yu captured Jingkou and made Chuo's son Lingshi a staff officer under the Jianwu commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Yu took Jingkou, he appointed Chuo's son Zhu Lingshi adjutant on the Jianwu staff.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊午朔，裕軍與吳甫之遇於江乘。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day wuwu, Yu's army met Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the new moon (day wuwu), Liu Yu's forces encountered Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 將戰，齡石言於裕曰：「齡石世受桓氏厚恩，不欲以兵刃相向，乞在軍後。」

translations.literal: About to give battle, Lingshi spoke to Yu, saying, "Lingshi through the generations received the Huan clan's thick kindness; I do not wish to confront them with blades—I beg to be in the army's rear."
translations.idiomatic: As battle was about to begin, Zhu Lingshi said to Liu Yu, "My family owes the Huans a deep debt. I cannot bear to cross blades with them. Let me serve in the rear."

sentences.zh: 裕義而許之。

translations.literal: Yu, out of righteousness, granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his loyalty, Liu Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 甫之，玄驍將也，其兵甚銳。

translations.literal: Fuzhi was Xuan's fierce general; his troops were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Fuzhi was one of Huan Xuan's finest commanders, and his men fought with exceptional bite.

sentences.zh: 裕手執長刀，大呼以沖之，眾皆披靡，即斬甫之，進至羅落橋。

translations.literal: Yu in hand grasped a long knife, greatly shouted to charge them; the masses all broke and scattered—forthwith he beheaded Fuzhi and advanced to Luoluo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu gripped a long saber and charged with a thunderous cry. The enemy ranks broke before him; he cut down Fuzhi on the spot and pressed on to Luoluo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 皇甫敷帥數千人逆戰，寧遠將軍檀賃之敗死。

translations.literal: Huangfu Fu led several thousand men to oppose in battle; the distant-watching General Tan Pinzhi was defeated and died.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Fu came against him with several thousand men. The Ningyuan general Tan Pingzhi was killed in defeat.

sentences.zh: 裕進戰彌厲，敷圍之數重，裕倚大樹挺戰。

translations.literal: Yu pressed the battle ever more fiercely; Fu surrounded him in several rings; Yu leaned on a great tree and fought with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu fought all the harder. Fu hemmed him in layer upon layer until Liu Yu stood with his back to a great tree and fought on.

sentences.zh: 敷曰：「汝欲作何死！」

translations.literal: Fu said, "You wish to die how!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu shouted, "What kind of death do you want?"

sentences.zh: 拔戟將刺之，裕瞋目叱之，敷辟易。

translations.literal: He drew his halberd and was about to stab him; Yu glared and shouted at him—Fu fell back.
translations.idiomatic: He leveled his halberd to run Liu Yu through, but Liu Yu fixed him with a glare and a roar. Fu shrank back.

sentences.zh: 裕黨俄至，射敷中額而踣，裕援刀直進。

translations.literal: Yu's partisans soon arrived, shot Fu in the forehead, and he fell; Yu seized his knife and pressed straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's men arrived in moments. An arrow struck Fu in the forehead and he toppled. Liu Yu drove his blade forward.

sentences.zh: 敷曰：「君有天命，以子孫為托。」

translations.literal: Fu said, "My lord has Heaven's mandate—take my sons and grandsons as your charge."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Fu said, "You bear Heaven's mandate. I entrust my sons to you."

sentences.zh: 裕斬之，厚撫其孤。

translations.literal: Yu beheaded him and richly comforted his orphans.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu killed him, then treated his orphaned children with generous care.

sentences.zh: 裕以檀憑之所領兵配參軍檀祗。

translations.literal: Yu allotted the troops that Tan Pingzhi had commanded to the staff officer Tan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu assigned the troops formerly under Tan Pingzhi to his aide Tan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 祗，憑之之從子也。。

translations.literal: Zhi was Pingzhi's younger clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhi was a cousin of Tan Pingzhi.

sentences.zh: 玄聞二將死，大懼，召諸道術人推算及為厭勝。

translations.literal: Xuan heard that the two generals had died and was greatly afraid; he summoned the various practitioners of the Way to calculate and perform suppressive rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan learned both generals were dead, terror seized him. He called in diviners and ritual specialists to cast his fate and ward off ill luck.

sentences.zh: 問群臣曰：「朕其敗乎？」

translations.literal: He asked the court ministers, "Will I be defeated?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked his ministers, "Am I doomed to lose?"

sentences.zh: 吏部郎曹靖之對曰：「民怨神怒，臣實懼焉。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel officer Cao Jingzhi answered, saying, "The people resent and the spirits rage—I, your servant, am truly afraid."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzhi, director of the Ministry of Personnel, replied, "The people are bitter and the gods are angry. I tremble for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「民或可怨，神何為怒？」

translations.literal: Xuan said, "The people may perhaps resent—but why would the spirits rage?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan said, "The common folk may hate me, but why would the gods be angry?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「晉氏宗廟，飄泊江濱，大楚之祭，上不及祖，此其所以怒也。」

translations.literal: He answered, "The Jin clan's ancestral temple drifts along the river banks; the Great Chu sacrifices do not reach to the ancestors—this is why they rage."
translations.idiomatic: Cao answered, "The Jin ancestral shrines still wander displaced along the Yangtze. Your Great Chu rites honor no forebears of the dynasty. That is why Heaven is enraged."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「卿何不諫？」

translations.literal: Xuan said, "Why did you not remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan said, "Why did you never speak up?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「輦上君子皆以為堯、舜之世，臣何敢言！」

translations.literal: He answered, "The gentlemen aboard the imperial carriage all took it to be the age of Yao and Shun—how could I, your servant, dare speak!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Everyone around the throne called this an age of Yao and Shun. How could a humble officer dare speak out?"

sentences.zh: 玄默然。

translations.literal: Xuan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan said nothing.

sentences.zh: 使桓謙及游擊將軍何澹之屯東陵，侍中、後將軍卞范之屯覆舟山西，眾合二萬。。

translations.literal: He sent Huan Qian and the roaming-strike General He Danzhi to encamp at Dongling, and the attendant-in-ordinary and rear general Bian Fanzhi to encamp west of Fuzhou Mountain—troops together twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Huan Qian and the mobile corps commander He Danzhi at Dongling, and the Palace Attendant and rear general Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain, twenty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 己未，裕軍食畢，悉棄其餘糧，進至覆舟山東，使羸弱登山，張旗幟為疑兵，數道並前，佈滿山谷。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, when Yu's army had finished eating, they wholly cast away the remaining grain, advanced to east of Fuzhou Mountain, made the weak climb the mountain and spread banners as decoy troops, and several routes advanced together, arrayed full through valley and hill.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, after his troops had eaten, Liu Yu discarded their leftover grain and marched east of Fuzhou Mountain. He sent the weaker men up the slopes with banners to feign a vast host, then advanced on many paths until every gorge seemed full of soldiers.

sentences.zh: 玄偵候者還，云「裕軍四塞，不知多少。」

translations.literal: Xuan's scouts returned, saying, "Yu's army seals on four sides—none know how many."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's scouts reported that Liu Yu's forces had closed in on every side, and no one could tell their number.

sentences.zh: 玄益憂恐，遣武衛將軍庾賾之帥精卒副援諸軍。

translations.literal: Xuan grew ever more worried and afraid; he dispatched the martial-guard general Yu Yizhi to lead picked troops as deputy relief for the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: His fear deepened. He sent the Martial Guard general Yu Yizhi forward with an elite detachment to reinforce the line.

sentences.zh: 謙等士卒多北府人，素畏伏裕，莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: Qian and the others' soldiers were mostly men of the Northern Headquarters, who from of old feared and submitted to Yu; none had fighting will.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Qian's troops were veterans of the Northern Headquarters, long accustomed to fear Liu Yu. They had no heart to fight.

sentences.zh: 裕與劉毅等分為數隊，進突謙陳；

translations.literal: Yu together with Liu Yi and others divided into several teams and advanced in sudden attack on Qian's battle formation;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu and Liu Yi split into columns and struck Qian's line;

sentences.zh: 裕以身先之，將士皆殊死戰，無不一當百，呼聲動天地。

translations.literal: Yu with his body led the way; officers and soldiers all fought to the death without exception—one matched a hundred—and their shouts moved heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu led from the front. Every man fought as if one could hold off a hundred. Their battle cries shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 時東北風急，因縱火焚之，煙炎慓天，鼓噪之音震動京邑，謙等諸軍大潰。。

translations.literal: At that time the northeast wind was fierce; accordingly they loosed fire to burn them—smoke and flame billowed to the sky; drum and war-cry sounds shook the capital district; Qian and the others' various armies were greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce northeast wind arose. Liu Yu set the field ablaze. Smoke and flame towered to the sky; drums and shouts rolled through the capital. Qian's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 玄時雖遣軍拒裕，而走意已決，潛使領軍將軍殷仲文具舟於石頭；

translations.literal: Xuan then, though he had sent troops to oppose Yu, had already decided on flight; secretly he had the commanding-general Yin Zhongwen prepare boats at Shitou;
translations.idiomatic: Though Huan Xuan still sent armies against Liu Yu, he had already chosen flight. In secret he ordered the chief commander Yin Zhongwen to ready boats at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 聞謙等敗，帥親信數千人，聲言赴戰，遂將其子昇，兄子浚出南掖門。

translations.literal: Hearing that Qian and the others were defeated, he led several thousand close followers, loudly declaring he was going to battle, then took his son Sheng and his elder brother's son Jun and went out the South Fringe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Qian was beaten, he gathered several thousand trusted men, claimed he was riding to the fight, and fled with his son Sheng and nephew Jun through the South Fringe Gate.

sentences.zh: 遇前相國參軍胡籓，執馬鞚諫曰：「今羽林射手猶有八百，皆是義戰，西人受累世之恩，不驅令一戰，一旦捨此，欲安之乎！」

translations.literal: He met the former chief administrator of state Hu Fan, who grasped the horse's cheek-strap and remonstrated, saying, "Now the armored archers still have eight hundred—all are volunteers for righteousness. Westerners have received generations of grace—will you not drive them to one battle? Once you cast this aside, where will you find peace!"
translations.idiomatic: At the gate he met the former chief minister's aide Hu Fan, who seized the bridle and pleaded, "Eight hundred elite archers still stand ready—all volunteers. These Westerners owe your house generations of favor. Will you not order them into one last fight? If you abandon them now, where can you go in safety?"

sentences.zh: 玄不對，但舉策指天，因鞭馬而走，西趨石頭，與仲文等浮江南走。

translations.literal: Xuan did not answer, only raised his whip pointing at heaven, then whipped his horse and ran; he rushed west toward Shitou, and with Zhongwen and the others floated down the river and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan made no reply. He lifted his whip toward the sky, then lashed his horse and fled west to Shitou, where he and Zhongwen took boats downriver and fled south.

sentences.zh: 經日不食，左右進粗飯，玄咽不能下，昇抱其胸而撫之，玄悲不自勝。。

translations.literal: For a whole day he did not eat; attendants offered coarse rice—Xuan could not swallow; Sheng embraced his chest and comforted him; Xuan was overcome with grief beyond bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He went a full day without food. When attendants brought coarse fare, he could not swallow. His son Sheng held him and soothed him until Xuan broke down in uncontrollable grief.

sentences.zh: 裕入建康，王仲德抱元德子方回出候裕，裕於馬上抱方回與仲德對哭。

translations.literal: Yu entered Jiankang; Wang Zhongde held Yuan De's son Fanghui and came out to await Yu; Yu on horseback held Fanghui and faced Zhongde in mutual weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu entered Jiankang. Wang Zhongde brought out Zhang Yuande's son Fanghui to meet him. Liu Yu lifted the boy onto his saddle, and the two men wept facing each other.

sentences.zh: 追贈元德給事中，以仲德為中軍參軍。

translations.literal: He pursued posthumous conferral on Yuan De as gentleman attendant-at-court and made Zhongde a central-army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He granted Zhang Yuande the posthumous rank of Gentleman Attendant-at-Court and appointed Zhongde adjutant on the central army staff.

sentences.zh: 裕止桓謙故營，遣劉鐘據東府。

translations.literal: Yu halted at Huan Qian's former camp and sent Liu Zhong to occupy the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu encamped at Huan Qian's former site and sent Liu Zhong to hold the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 庚申，裕屯石頭城，立留台百官，焚桓溫神主於宣陽門外，造晉新主，納於太廟。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, Yu encamped at Shitou city, established the remaining court officials, burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, and made new Jin spirit tablets and installed them in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he took Shitou, reconstituted the provisional court, burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet before Xuanyang Gate, fashioned new tablets for the Jin imperial house, and installed them in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將追玄，尚書王嘏帥百官奉迎乘輿，誅玄宗族在建康者。

translations.literal: He sent the various generals to pursue Xuan; the Minister over the Masses Wang Tan led the hundred officials to welcome the imperial carriage, and executed Xuan's clan members in Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched generals to hunt Huan Xuan. Minister over the Masses Wang Tan led the court to welcome the emperor home while Xuan's kinsmen in the capital were put to death.

sentences.zh: 裕使臧熹入宮，收圖書、器物，封閉府庫；

translations.literal: Yu sent Zang Xi to enter the palace to gather books, implements, and seal and close the treasuries;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Zang Xi into the palace to collect books, regalia, and stores and to seal the treasuries;

sentences.zh: 有金飾樂器，裕問熹：「卿得無慾此乎？」

translations.literal: There were gold-decorated musical instruments; Yu asked Xi, "You would not desire these, would you?"
translations.idiomatic: Among them were instruments gilded in gold. Liu Yu teased Xi, "You aren't tempted by these, are you?"

sentences.zh: 熹正色曰：「皇上幽逼，播越非所，將軍首建大義，劬勞王家，雖復不肖，實無情於樂。」

translations.literal: Xi with stern countenance said, "The emperor suffers seclusion, driven to wander not his place; the general first raised great righteousness, toiling for the royal house—though again I am unworthy, truly I have no feeling for music."
translations.idiomatic: Xi answered gravely, "Our sovereign has been held captive and driven from his rightful place. You, General, raised this righteous cause and labor for the dynasty. Unworthy as I am, I have no heart for music."

sentences.zh: 裕笑曰：「聊以戲卿耳。」

translations.literal: Yu laughed and said, "Just to tease you, that's all."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu laughed. "Only teasing you."

sentences.zh: 熹，燾之弟也。。

translations.literal: Xi was Tao's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi was the younger brother of Zang Tao.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，玄司徒王謐與眾議推裕領揚州，裕固辭，乃以謐為侍中、領司徒、揚州刺史、錄尚書事，謐推裕為使持節、都督揚、徐、兗、豫、青、冀、幽、并八州諸軍事、徐州刺史，劉毅為青州刺史，何無忌為琅邪內史，孟昶為丹陽尹，劉道規為義昌太守。。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Xuan's Minister of Education Wang Mi together with the assembly deliberated and pushed Yu to head Yangzhou; Yu firmly declined—thereupon they made Mi attendant-in-ordinary, bearing Minister of Education, Yangzhou inspector, recording Secretariat affairs; Mi pushed Yu as commissioner bearing credentials, area commander of the eight provinces Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, and inspector of Xuzhou; Liu Yi as Qingzhou inspector; He Wuji as Langye interior minister; Meng Chang as Danyang magistrate; Liu Daogui as Yichang grand warden.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Wang Mi, whom Huan Xuan had made Minister of Education, joined the court in urging Liu Yu to take Yangzhou. Liu Yu refused firmly. Mi was instead made Palace Attendant, Minister of Education, governor of Yangzhou, and chief of Secretariat affairs; he then pressed Liu Yu to accept commission with full credentials as commander-in-chief over Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, and as governor of Xuzhou. Liu Yi was named governor of Qingzhou, He Wuji interior minister of Langye, Meng Chang magistrate of Danyang, and Liu Daogui grand warden of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 裕始至建康，諸大處分皆委於劉穆之，倉猝立定，無不允愜。

translations.literal: When Yu had first arrived at Jiankang, the various weighty dispositions were all entrusted to Liu Muzhi; in haste he set things firm, without any not accordant and satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu first reached Jiankang, nearly every important decision went to Liu Muzhi. In the rush of those days Muzhi settled affairs so swiftly that none went unsatisfied.

sentences.zh: 裕遂托以腹心，動止咨焉；

translations.literal: Yu thereupon entrusted him as belly-and-heart; in motion and rest he consulted him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu made him his right hand and consulted him on every move;

sentences.zh: 穆之亦竭節盡誠，無所遣隱。

translations.literal: Muzhi also exhausted his integrity and utmost loyalty, in nothing holding back concealment.
translations.idiomatic: and Muzhi in turn served with absolute loyalty, hiding nothing.

sentences.zh: 時晉政寬馳，綱紀不立，豪族陵縱，小民窮蹙，重以司馬元顯政令違舛。

translations.literal: At that time Jin government was wide and slack, statutes and discipline not established; powerful clans overawed and indulged, common people were impoverished and pressed—and moreover Secretary of State Yuan Xian's government orders were contrary and mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court had long been lax: law and custom had rotted, great families bullied as they pleased, and the poor were crushed under debt—made worse by Sima Yuanxian's perverse edicts.

sentences.zh: 桓玄雖欲厘整，而科條繁密，眾莫之從。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan though wished to rectify and order, yet codes and articles were numerous and dense; the masses did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had tried to reform the realm, but his code grew dense and intricate until no one could obey it.

sentences.zh: 穆之斟酌時宜，隨方矯正；

translations.literal: Muzhi weighed the time's fitness and followed directions to correct;
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi judged each abuse by the standards of the moment and bent policy back toward order;

sentences.zh: 裕以身范物，先以威禁；

translations.literal: Yu with his person modeled things and first used authority and prohibition;
translations.idiomatic: while Liu Yu himself led by example, enforcing discipline with stern will.

sentences.zh: 內外百官皆肅然奉職，不盈旬日，風俗頓改。。

translations.literal: Inner and outer hundred officials all solemnly fulfilled office; not full ten days—and custom abruptly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days officials inside and outside the court were performing their duties in earnest, and the tone of the capital changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 初，諸葛長民至豫州，失期，不得發。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Zhuge Changmin reached Yuzhou, missed the period, and could not set out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhuge Changmin had reached Yuzhou but missed his muster date and could not march.

sentences.zh: 刁逵執長民，檻車送桓玄。

translations.literal: Diao Kui arrested Changmin and sent him in a caged cart to Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Kui seized him and sent him toward Huan Xuan in a prisoner cart.

sentences.zh: 至當利而玄敗，送人共破檻出長民，還趣歷陽。

translations.literal: When they reached Dangli, Xuan was defeated; the escort together broke the cage and released Changmin, and he returned in haste to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Dangli word came that Huan Xuan was beaten. The escort broke open the cart and freed Changmin, who hurried back to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 逵棄城走，為其下所執，斬於石頭，子侄無少長皆死，唯赦其季弟給事中騁。

translations.literal: Kui abandoned the city and fled; was seized by his subordinates and beheaded at Shitou—sons and nephews without regard to age and youth all died; only his youngest younger brother, gentleman attendant-at-court Pi, was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Kui fled the city but was caught by his own men and executed at Shitou. Sons and nephews of every age were killed; only his youngest brother Pi, a Gentleman Attendant-at-Court, was spared.

sentences.zh: 逵故吏匿其弟子雍送洛陽，秦王興以為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Kui's former clerks hid his younger brother's son Yong and sent him to Luoyang; the King of Qin, Xing, made him crown prince household attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's old retainers hid his nephew Yong and smuggled him to Luoyang, where Yao Xing of Later Qin made him an attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 裕以魏詠之為豫州刺史，鎮歷陽，諸葛長民為宣城內史。。

translations.literal: Yu made Wei Yongzhi inspector of Yuzhou, garrisoning Liyang; Zhuge Changmin was made Xuancheng interior minister.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu named Wei Yongzhi governor of Yuzhou with his seat at Liyang, and Zhuge Changmin interior minister of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 初，裕名微位薄，輕狡無行，盛流皆不與相知，惟王謐獨奇貴之，謂裕曰：「卿當為一代英雄。」

translations.literal: At the beginning, Yu's fame was slight and position thin, light and crafty without conduct; eminent currents all did not know him—only Wang Mi alone wondered at and prized him, saying to Yu, "You will surely be a hero of an age."
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days Liu Yu was unknown and lowly, with a reputation for rowdiness. The great families would not look at him—only Wang Mi saw something extraordinary in him and said, "You are destined to be a hero of your age."

sentences.zh: 裕嘗與刁逵樗蒲，不時輸直，逵縛之馬柳。

translations.literal: Yu once with Diao Kui played at backgammon; when the stakes came due he did not pay; Kui bound him to the horse pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Yu gambled at backgammon with Diao Kui and failed to pay when he lost. Kui had him tied to the hitching post.

sentences.zh: 謐見之，責逵而釋之，代之還直。

translations.literal: Mi saw it, blamed Kui and released him, and in his stead repaid the stakes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi saw it, rebuked Kui, freed Liu Yu, and paid the debt himself.

sentences.zh: 由是裕深憾逵而德謐。。

translations.literal: Because of this Yu deeply resented Kui and was grateful to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Liu Yu bore a deep grudge against Kui and a deep debt to Mi.

sentences.zh: 蕭方等曰：夫蛟龍潛伏，魚蝦褻之。

translations.literal: Xiao Fangdeng said, "When the flood dragon lies hidden, fish and shrimp profane it."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Fangde remarked, "When a flood dragon lies hidden, even shrimp and minnows dare insult it."

sentences.zh: 是以漢高赦雍齒，魏武免梁鵠，安可以布衣之嫌而成萬乘之隙也！

translations.literal: For this reason Han Gaozu pardoned Yong Chi, and Wei Wu released Liang Hu—how can one take a common-cloth grudge and make it a gap for the ten-thousand chariots!
translations.idiomatic: That is why Emperor Gaozu of Han pardoned Yong Chi and Cao Cao spared Liang Hu. How can a squabble among commoners be allowed to seed a feud against the throne?

sentences.zh: 今王謐為公，刁逵亡族，酬恩報怨，何其狹哉！。

translations.literal: Now Wang Mi is made duke, Diao Kui's clan perished—repaying kindness and repaying grudge—how narrow!
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Mi is made a duke while Diao Kui's house is exterminated. To reward a friend and destroy an enemy in one stroke—how small-minded!

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射王愉及子荊州刺史綏謀襲裕，事洩，族誅，綏弟子慧龍為僧彬所匿，得免。。

translations.literal: Minister of Works left vice-minister Wang Yu and his son Jingzhou inspector Sui plotted to raid Yu; the affair leaked; the clan was executed and exterminated—Sui's younger brother's son Huilong was hidden by monk Bin and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and his son Sui, governor of Jingzhou, plotted a surprise attack on Liu Yu. When the plot was exposed, their clan was wiped out. Sui's nephew Hui'long was hidden by the monk Senbin and survived.

sentences.zh: 魏以中土蕭條，詔縣戶不滿百者罷之。。

translations.literal: Wei, because the central land was desolate and stripped, ordered that counties with households not reaching a hundred be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei, finding the heartland depopulated, ordered any county with fewer than a hundred households dissolved.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，劉裕遷鎮東府。。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Liu Yu moved his garrison to the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Liu Yu shifted his headquarters to the Eastern Palace compound.

sentences.zh: 桓玄至尋陽，郭昶之給其器用、兵力。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan reached Xunyang; Guo Changzhi supplied his implements and military strength.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan reached Xunyang, where Guo Changzhi furnished him with supplies and troops.

sentences.zh: 辛未，玄逼帝西上，劉毅帥何無忌、劉道規等諸軍追之。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Xuan compelled the emperor to go west; Liu Yi led He Wuji, Liu Daogui, and the others' armies in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he forced the emperor westward. Liu Yi marched in pursuit with He Wuji, Liu Daogui, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 玄留龍驤將軍何澹之、前將軍郭銓與郭昶之守湓口。

translations.literal: Xuan left the dragon-fierce General He Danzhi and the former general Guo Quan together with Guo Changzhi to defend Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan left the Dragon-Fierce General He Danzhi and the former general Guo Quan, with Guo Changzhi, to hold Penkou.

sentences.zh: 玄於道自作《起居注》，敘討劉裕事，自謂經略舉無遺策，諸軍違節度，以致奔敗。

translations.literal: On the road Xuan himself composed the "Records of the Sovereign's Coming and Going," narrating the campaign against Liu Yu—he called his strategy and planning wholly without omitted plans; the various armies violated regulations and discipline, thereby bringing flight and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he drafted his own "Imperial Diary," recounting the war against Liu Yu. He claimed his strategy had been flawless and blamed the armies for disobeying orders—thereby turning victory to rout.

sentences.zh: 專覃思著述，不暇與群下議時事。

translations.literal: He alone immersed his thoughts in writing and composing, with no leisure to discuss current affairs with the assembled subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He buried himself in writing and had no time to consult his officers on the crisis at hand.

sentences.zh: 《起居注》既成，宣示遠近。。

translations.literal: When the "Records of the Sovereign's Coming and Going" was finished, he displayed and announced it far and near.
translations.idiomatic: When the diary was done, he published it for all the realm to read.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，劉裕稱受帝密詔，以武陵王遵承製總百官行事，加侍中、大將軍，因大赦，惟桓玄一族不宥。。

translations.literal: On day bingxu, Liu Yu claimed to have received the emperor's secret edict, making the Prince of Wuling, Zun, receive the imperial regimen and oversee all officials' affairs, adding Palace Attendant and Grand General; thereby a great amnesty—only Huan Xuan's clan was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Liu Yu announced that he held a secret edict from the emperor appointing Prince Zun of Wuling to govern in the emperor's name and command all offices. Zun was made Palace Attendant and Grand General, and a general amnesty was proclaimed—except for the house of Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣、高雅之結青州大姓及鮮卑豪帥，謀殺南燕主備德，推司馬休之為主。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan and Gao Yazhi joined Qingzhou great clans and Xianbei chieftains, plotting to kill the Southern Yan ruler Murong De and install Sima Xiuzhi as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan and Gao Yazhi rallied great Qingzhou families and Xianbei chiefs in a plot to assassinate Murong De of Southern Yan and set up Sima Xiuzhi as their leader.

sentences.zh: 備德以劉軌為司空，甚寵信之。

translations.literal: Murong De made Liu Gui Minister of Works and greatly favored and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De had appointed Liu Gui Minister of Works and held him in high favor.

sentences.zh: 雅之欲邀軌同謀，敬宣曰：「劉公衰老，有安齊之志，不可告也。」

translations.literal: Yazhi wished to invite Gui into the plot together. Jingxuan said, "Lord Liu is aged and has a mind to settle in Qi—this cannot be told to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yazhi wanted to bring Liu Gui into the conspiracy. Jingxuan objected: "Liu Gui is old and content in Qi. We must not tell him."

sentences.zh: 雅之卒告之，軌不從。

translations.literal: Yazhi in the end told him; Gui would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yazhi told him anyway. Liu Gui refused to join.

sentences.zh: 謀頗洩，敬宣等南走，南燕人收軌，殺之，追及雅之，又殺之。

translations.literal: The plot leaked considerably; Jingxuan and the others fled south. Southern Yan men seized Gui and killed him, overtook Yazhi, and killed him too.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked. Jingxuan and his party fled south. Southern Yan authorities arrested Liu Gui and executed him, then caught Yazhi on the road and killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 敬宣、休之至淮、泗間，聞桓玄敗，遂來歸，劉裕以敬宣為晉陵太守。。

translations.literal: Jingxuan and Xiuzhi reached the Huai and Si region, heard Huan Xuan had been defeated, then came to submit. Liu Yu made Jingxuan Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan and Xiuzhi reached the Huai and Si country. Learning of Huan Xuan's defeat, they came over to Liu Yu, who appointed Jingxuan Administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 南燕主備德聞桓玄敗，命北地王鐘等將兵欲取江南，會備德有疾而止。。

translations.literal: The Southern Yan ruler Murong De, hearing Huan Xuan was defeated, ordered the Prince of Beituo, Zhong, and others to lead troops intending to seize Jiangnan; it happened Murong De fell ill and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De of Southern Yan, hearing of Huan Xuan's fall, ordered Prince Zhong of Beituo and others to march on Jiangnan—but Murong De fell ill and the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己丑，武陵王遵入居東宮，內外畢敬；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jichou—the Prince of Wuling, Zun, entered and dwelt in the Eastern Palace; inside and outside all showed respect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jichou, Prince Zun of Wuling took up residence in the Eastern Palace, and court and camp alike paid him full deference.

sentences.zh: 遷除百官稱制書，教稱令書。

translations.literal: Promotions and dismissals of the hundred officials were called "regimen documents"; edicts were called "order letters."
translations.idiomatic: Appointments and removals were issued as regimen edicts; imperial instructions went out as order letters.

sentences.zh: 以司馬休之監荊、益、梁、寧、秦、雍六州諸軍事、領荊州刺史。。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi was made overseer of military affairs for the six provinces Jing, Yi, Liang, Ning, Qin, and Yong, and concurrently Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi was made commander over military affairs in Jing, Yi, Liang, Ning, Qin, and Yong, and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，桓玄挾帝至江陵，桓石康納之。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, Huan Xuan took the emperor in escort to Jiangling; Huan Shikang received them in.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Huan Xuan brought the emperor to Jiangling, where Huan Shikang received them into the city.

sentences.zh: 玄更署置百官，以卞范之為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Xuan anew appointed and installed the hundred officials, making Bian Fanzhi Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan reconstituted the bureaucracy and named Bian Fanzhi Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 自以奔敗之後，恐威令不行，乃更增峻刑罰，眾益離怨。

translations.literal: Since after his flight and defeat he feared his authority and orders would not be obeyed, he then further increased harsh punishments; the masses grew more alienated and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: After his rout he feared his orders would no longer be obeyed, so he tightened punishments still further—and his followers only grew more estranged.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文諫，玄怒曰：「今以諸將失律，天文不利，故還都舊楚；

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen remonstrated. Xuan angrily said, "Now because the various generals violated discipline and the heavenly signs were unfavorable, therefore I return the capital to old Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen urged restraint. Huan Xuan snapped, "Our generals broke discipline and the heavens turned against us—that is why we withdrew to old Chu.

sentences.zh: 而群小紛紛，妄興異議！

translations.literal: Yet the petty crowd clamor and rashly raise contrary opinions!
translations.idiomatic: And now petty men chatter and dare raise foolish objections!

sentences.zh: 方當糾之以猛，未可施之以寬也。」

translations.literal: Just now one should correct them with severity—it is not yet possible to apply leniency to them."
translations.idiomatic: This is the hour for stern correction, not for clemency."

sentences.zh: 荊、江諸郡聞玄播越，有上表奔問起居者，玄皆不受，更令所在賀遷新都。。

translations.literal: The various commanderies of Jing and Jiang, hearing Xuan had been driven into exile, some submitted memorials rushing to inquire after his well-being—Xuan would accept none of them and instead ordered each place to congratulate the move to the new capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jing and Jiang commanderies heard that Huan Xuan had fled west, some sent memorials asking after his health. He refused them all and ordered each district to congratulate him on establishing his new capital instead.

sentences.zh: 初，王謐為玄佐命元臣，玄之受禪，謐手解帝璽綬；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Mi was Xuan's founding minister and chief aide; at Xuan's receiving the abdication, Mi with his own hands removed the emperor's seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi had been Huan Xuan's chief counselor in founding the usurpation; when Xuan took the throne, it was Mi who removed the imperial seal and cord from the emperor's waist.

sentences.zh: 乃玄敗，眾謂謐宜誅，劉裕特保全之。

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated, the multitude said Mi ought to be executed; Liu Yu especially preserved him.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's defeat many demanded Mi's death, but Liu Yu deliberately spared him.

sentences.zh: 劉毅嘗因朝會，問謐璽綬所在。

translations.literal: Liu Yi once at a court assembly asked Mi where the seal and cord were.
translations.idiomatic: At a court session Liu Yi publicly asked Mi where the imperial seal and cord were kept.

sentences.zh: 謐內不自安，逃奔曲阿。

translations.literal: Mi inwardly was not at ease and fled to Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, unable to bear the pressure, fled to Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 裕箋白武陵王，迎還復位。。

translations.literal: Yu by letter informed the Prince of Wuling, who welcomed him back to restore his position.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu wrote to Prince Zun of Wuling, who had Mi brought back and reinstated.

sentences.zh: 桓玄兄子歆引氐帥楊秋寇歷陽，魏詠之帥諸葛長民、劉敬宣、劉鐘共擊破之，斬楊秋於練固。。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan's elder brother's son Xin led the Di chieftain Yang Qiu to raid Liyang. Wei Yongzhi led Zhuge Changmin, Liu Jingxuan, and Liu Zhong together to strike and defeat them, beheading Yang Qiu at Liangu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xin's nephew led the Di chief Yang Qiu against Liyang. Wei Yongzhi, with Zhuge Changmin, Liu Jingxuan, and Liu Zhong, routed them and beheaded Yang Qiu at Liangu.

sentences.zh: 玄使武衛將軍庾稚祖、江夏太守桓道恭帥數千人就何澹之等共守湓口。

translations.literal: Xuan sent the Martial Guard General Yu Zhizu and the Jiangxia Administrator Huan Daogong leading several thousand men to join He Danzhi and the others in jointly defending Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan sent the Martial Guard General Yu Zhizu and Jiangxia prefect Huan Daogong with several thousand men to reinforce He Danzhi at Penkou.

sentences.zh: 何無忌、劉道規至桑落洲，庚戌，澹之等引舟師逆戰。

translations.literal: He Wuji and Liu Daogui reached Sangluo Isle. On day gengxu, Danzhi and the others led the river fleet to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji and Liu Daogui reached Sangluo Isle. On gengxu, He Danzhi brought the fleet out to fight.

sentences.zh: 澹之常所乘舫羽儀旗幟甚盛，無忌曰：「賊帥必不居此，欲詐我耳，宜亟攻之。」

translations.literal: The barge Danzhi usually rode had very grand insignia, banners, and flags. Wuji said, "The rebel commander surely will not be aboard this one—he means to deceive us. We should attack it at once."
translations.idiomatic: He Danzhi's usual flagship flew lavish banners and pennants. He Wuji said, "Their commander won't be on that ship—it's a decoy. Strike it now."

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「澹之不在其中，得之無益。」

translations.literal: The crowd said, "If Danzhi is not among them, taking it is no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Others objected: "If Danzhi isn't aboard, capturing the ship gains us nothing."

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「今眾寡不敵，戰無全勝，澹之既不居此舫，戰士必弱，我以勁兵攻之，必得之；

translations.literal: Wuji said, "Now our numbers cannot match theirs; in battle there is no complete victory. Since Danzhi is not on this barge, the fighters must be weak. If we attack with crack troops, we are sure to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji replied, "We're outnumbered—we can't expect a clean victory. If Danzhi isn't on that vessel, its crew will be second-rate. Hit it with our best troops and we'll take it.

sentences.zh: 得之，則彼勢沮而我氣倍，因而薄之，破賊必矣。」

translations.literal: If we take it, then their momentum will be broken and our spirit doubled; pressing on from there, breaking the rebels is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Once we have it, their spirit will break and ours will double. Press the attack then, and the enemy is finished."

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「善！」

translations.literal: Daogui said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daogui said, "Well said!"

sentences.zh: 遂往攻而得之，因傳呼曰：「已得何澹之矣」。

translations.literal: Thereupon they went to attack and took it, then passed the cry: "We have already got He Danzhi!"
translations.idiomatic: They attacked and captured the ship, then shouted through the fleet: "He Danzhi is ours!"

sentences.zh: 澹之軍中驚擾。

translations.literal: Within Danzhi's army there was alarm and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept He Danzhi's ranks.

sentences.zh: 無忌之眾亦以為然，乘勝進攻澹之等，大破之。

translations.literal: Wuji's troops also believed it true and, riding the victory, pressed the attack on Danzhi and the others, routing them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji's men believed the rumor too and pressed the advantage, shattering Danzhi's force.

sentences.zh: 無忌等克湓口，進據尋陽，遣使奉送宗廟主祏還京師。

translations.literal: Wuji and the others took Penkou, advanced to hold Xunyang, and sent envoys reverently escorting the ancestral temple spirit tablets back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji took Penkou and occupied Xunyang, then sent the imperial ancestral tablets back to the capital under escort.

sentences.zh: 加劉裕都督江州諸軍事。。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was added as overseer of military affairs for all Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was made commander over all military affairs in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 桑落之戰，胡籓所乘艦為官軍所燒，籓全鎧入水，潛行三十許步，乃得登岸。

translations.literal: In the battle of Sangluo, the warship Hu Fan rode was burned by the government army. Fan, in full armor, entered the water and secretly swam about thirty-odd paces before he could climb ashore.
translations.idiomatic: At Sangluo, Hu Fan's ship was set ablaze by the loyalist fleet. Clad in full armor he went overboard and swam underwater some thirty paces before reaching shore.

sentences.zh: 時江陵路已絕，乃還豫章。

translations.literal: At that time the road to Jiangling was already cut off, so he returned to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The route to Jiangling was closed, so he withdrew to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 劉裕素聞籓為人忠直，引參領軍軍事。。

translations.literal: Liu Yu had long heard Fan was a man loyal and upright and brought him in to participate in the Army Aide's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, who had long admired Fan's integrity, brought him into his staff as an adviser on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 桓玄收集荊州兵，曾未三旬，有眾二萬，樓船、器械甚盛。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan gathered Jingzhou troops; in less than thirty days he had a host of twenty thousand, with tower ships and weapons very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan rallied Jingzhou troops and in less than a month had twenty thousand men, with tower ships and arms in abundance.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，玄復帥諸軍挾帝東下，以苻宏領梁州刺史，為前鋒；

translations.literal: On day jiayin, Xuan again led the various armies, taking the emperor eastward. He made Fu Hong oversee Liangzhou as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Huan Xuan marched east again with the emperor in tow, placing Fu Hong in command of Liangzhou as his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又使散騎常侍徐放先行，說劉裕等曰：「若能旋軍散甲，當與之更始，各授位任，令不失分。」。

translations.literal: He also sent the Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Xu Fang ahead to say to Liu Yu and the others, "If you can turn your armies and disperse your armor, I will make a fresh start with you, each granting office and post, ensuring you do not lose your proper stations."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Regular Attendant Xu Fang ahead to tell Liu Yu: "Disband your armies and lay down your arms, and I will start anew with you—offices and ranks for all, none diminished in standing."

sentences.zh: 劉裕以諸葛長民都督淮北諸軍事，鎮山陽；

translations.literal: Liu Yu made Zhuge Changmin overseer of military affairs north of the Huai, garrisoning Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu made Zhuge Changmin commander north of the Huai and stationed him at Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 以劉敬宣為江州刺史。。

translations.literal: He made Liu Jingxuan Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liu Jingxuan Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 柔然可汗社侖從弟悅代大那謀殺社侖，不克，奔魏。。

translations.literal: The Rouran khan Shelun's younger cousin by the father's side, Yuedai Dana, plotted to kill Shelun but did not succeed and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuedai Dana, a cousin of the Rouran khan Shelun, plotted to kill him, failed, and fled to Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 燕王熙於友騰苑起逍遙宮，連房數百，鑿曲光海，盛夏，士卒不得休息，□曷死者大半。。

translations.literal: The Yan king Xi at Youteng Park raised the Free-and-Easy Palace, linked chambers numbering in the hundreds, and dug the Quguang Sea. In midsummer the soldiers could not rest; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xi of Later Yan built the Free-and-Easy Palace in Youteng Park—hundreds of linked chambers—and excavated the Quguang reservoir. In the height of summer the laborers were given no rest, and more than half of them died.

sentences.zh: 西涼世子譚卒。。

translations.literal: The Western Liang heir Tan died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tan, heir of Western Liang, died.

sentences.zh: 劉毅、何無忌、劉道規、下邳太守平昌孟懷玉帥眾自尋陽西上，五月，癸酉，與桓玄遇於崢嶸洲。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, He Wuji, Liu Daogui, and the Xiapi Administrator of Pingchang Meng Huaiyu led the host west from Xunyang. Fifth month, day guiyou—they met Huan Xuan at Zhengrong Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, He Wuji, Liu Daogui, and Meng Huaiyu of Pingchang, prefect of Xiapi, marched west from Xunyang. In the fifth month, on guiyou, they met Huan Xuan at Zhengrong Isle.

sentences.zh: 毅等兵不滿萬人，而玄戰士數萬，眾憚之，欲退還尋陽。

translations.literal: Yi's troops were not full ten thousand, while Xuan's fighting men numbered tens of thousands. The crowd feared them and wished to withdraw back to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's force numbered fewer than ten thousand against Huan Xuan's tens of thousands. The army wavered and wanted to fall back on Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 道規曰：「不可！

translations.literal: Daogui said, "It cannot be done!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Daogui said, "We must not!

sentences.zh: 彼眾我寡，強弱異勢，今若畏懦不進，必為所乘，雖至尋陽，豈能自固！

translations.literal: They are many, we few; strong and weak differ in momentum. If now from fear and cowardice we do not advance, we are sure to be ridden by them—even if we reach Xunyang, how could we secure ourselves!
translations.idiomatic: They outnumber us; the odds are against us. If we shrink back now, they will run us down—even at Xunyang we could not hold.

sentences.zh: 玄雖竊名雄豪，內實恇怯；

translations.literal: Xuan, though he usurped the name of a bold hero, inwardly was in truth timid and cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan plays the conqueror, but at heart he is a coward.

sentences.zh: 加之已經奔敗，眾無固心。

translations.literal: Moreover he had already suffered flight and defeat; the host had no firm heart.
translations.idiomatic: He has already been routed once; his men have no stomach for another fight.

sentences.zh: 決機兩陣，將雄者克，不在眾也。」

translations.literal: When fate is decided between two battle lines, the commander who is bold conquers—it lies not in numbers."
translations.idiomatic: When two armies meet, the bolder general wins—not the larger one."

sentences.zh: 因麾眾先進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he waved the host to advance first.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the troops forward.

sentences.zh: 毅等從之。

translations.literal: Yi and the others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others followed.

sentences.zh: 玄常漾舸於舫側以備敗走，由是眾莫有鬥心。

translations.literal: Xuan constantly kept a light skiff rocking at the side of his barge to prepare for flight in defeat; because of this the host had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan kept a light boat tied alongside his flagship ready for escape, and his soldiers lost all heart to fight.

sentences.zh: 毅等乘風縱火，盡銳爭先，玄眾大潰，燒輜重夜遁。

translations.literal: Yi and the others rode the wind to set fires, with all their crack troops striving to be first. Xuan's host collapsed greatly; they burned the baggage train and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yi set the enemy fleet afire downwind and led the charge with every elite soldier. Huan Xuan's army broke; they burned their wagons and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 郭銓詣毅降。

translations.literal: Guo Quan went to Yi to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan came to Yi and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 玄故將劉統、馮稚等聚黨四百人襲破尋陽城。

translations.literal: Xuan's former generals Liu Tong, Feng Zhi, and others gathered a band of four hundred men and raided, breaking Xunyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's old officers Liu Tong and Feng Zhi rallied four hundred men and stormed Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 毅遣建威將軍劉懷隸討平之。

translations.literal: Yi sent the Establishing Might General Liu Huaisu to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent the Establishing Might General Liu Huaisu to crush them.

sentences.zh: 懷肅，懷敬之弟也。。

translations.literal: Huaisu was the younger brother of Huaijing.
translations.idiomatic: Huaisu was the younger brother of Liu Huaijing.

sentences.zh: 玄挾帝單舸西走，留永安何皇后及王皇后於巴陵。

translations.literal: Xuan took the emperor on a single skiff fleeing west, leaving the Yong'an Empress He and Empress Wang at Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan fled west with the emperor in a single boat, leaving Empress He of Yong'an and Empress Wang at Baling.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文時在玄艦，求出別船收集散卒，因叛玄，奉二後奔夏口，遂還建康。。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen was then on Xuan's warship; he asked to go out on a separate boat to gather scattered soldiers, then turned traitor to Xuan, escorting the two empresses to Xiakou, and then returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen, aboard Huan Xuan's ship, asked leave to take another vessel and gather stragglers—then defected, escorted both empresses to Xiakou, and returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 己卯，玄與帝入江陵。

translations.literal: On day jimao, Xuan and the emperor entered Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Huan Xuan and the emperor entered Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 馮該勸使更下戰，玄不從，欲奔漢中就桓希，而人情乖沮，號令不行。

translations.literal: Feng Gai urged him to go down and fight again; Xuan would not follow, wishing to flee to Hanzhong to join Huan Xi, but men's hearts were alienated and dejected and orders would not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Gai urged another stand; Huan Xuan refused and planned to flee to Hanzhong to join Huan Xi—but morale had collapsed and his orders went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，夜中，處分欲發，城內已亂，乃與親近腹心百餘人乘馬出城西走。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, in the middle of the night, as he arranged to depart, the city within was already in turmoil. Then with close confidants and trusted men, a hundred-odd, he mounted horses and went out the west gate fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, at midnight, as he prepared to leave, the city erupted in chaos. He rode out the west gate with a little over a hundred trusted followers.

sentences.zh: 至城門，左右於暗中斫玄，不中，其徒更相殺害，前後交橫。

translations.literal: Reaching the gate, attendants in the dark hacked at Xuan and missed. His followers then mutually slew one another, before and behind crossing in chaos.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate his guards struck at him in the dark and missed. His followers turned on one another in the crush.

sentences.zh: 玄僅得至船，左右分散，惟卞范之在側。。

translations.literal: Xuan barely reached the boat; attendants scattered—only Bian Fanzhi was at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan barely reached his boat. His attendants scattered; only Bian Fanzhi remained beside him.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，荊州別駕王康產奉帝入南郡府捨，太守王騰之帥文武為侍衛。。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, the Jingzhou Assistant Administrator Wang Kangchan escorted the emperor into the Nanjun government lodging; the Administrator Wang Tengzhi led civil and military officials as guards.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Jingzhou aide Wang Kangchan brought the emperor into the Nanjun government compound, while prefect Wang Tengzhi and his officials formed an escort.

sentences.zh: 玄將之漢中，屯騎校尉毛修之，璩之弟子也，誘玄入蜀，玄從之。

translations.literal: Xuan was about to go to Hanzhong. The Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Mao Xiuzhi—a nephew-disciple of Mao Jin—enticed Xuan to enter Shu, and Xuan followed.
translations.idiomatic: As Huan Xuan headed for Hanzhong, Colonel Mao Xiuzhi, a nephew of Mao Jin, persuaded him to flee into Shu instead—and Xuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 寧州刺史毛璠，璩之弟也，卒於官。

translations.literal: The Ningzhou Inspector Mao Fan was Mao Jin's younger brother and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Fan, governor of Ningzhou and younger brother of Mao Jin, had died in office.

sentences.zh: 璩使其兄孫祐之及參軍費恬帥數百人，送璠喪歸江陵，壬午，遇玄於枚回洲。

translations.literal: Jin sent his elder brother's grandson Youzhi and the staff officer Fei Tian leading several hundred men to escort Fan's coffin back to Jiangling. On day renwu they met Xuan at Meihui Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin sent his grandnephew Youzhi and aide Fei Tian with several hundred men to return Fan's coffin to Jiangling. On renwu they met Huan Xuan at Meihui Isle.

sentences.zh: 祐之、恬迎擊玄，矢下如雨，玄嬖人丁仙期、萬蓋等以身蔽玄，皆死。

translations.literal: Youzhi and Tian met and attacked Xuan; arrows fell like rain. Xuan's favorites Ding Xianqi, Wan Gai, and others used their bodies to shield Xuan—all died.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi and Tian attacked at once. Arrows fell like rain. Huan Xuan's favorites Ding Xianqi and Wan Gai shielded him with their bodies and were killed.

sentences.zh: 益州督護漢嘉馮遷抽刀，前欲擊玄，玄拔頭上玉導與之，曰：「汝何人，敢殺天子！」

translations.literal: The Yizhou Supervisor-Protector of Hanchang Feng Qian drew his blade and advanced wanting to strike Xuan. Xuan pulled the jade hairpin from his head and gave it to him, saying, "What man are you, daring to kill the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian of Hanchang, Yizhou protector, drew his sword and stepped forward. Huan Xuan pulled the jade pin from his hair and held it out. "Who are you," he cried, "to dare kill the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 遷曰：「我殺天子之賊耳！」

translations.literal: Qian said, "I kill the Son of Heaven's rebel, that is all!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian answered, "I kill the rebel who stole the throne!"

sentences.zh: 遂斬之，又斬桓石康、桓浚、庾□責之，執桓昇送江陵，斬於市。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beheaded him, and also beheaded Huan Shikang, Huan Jun, and Yu Yizhi; he seized Huan Sheng and sent him to Jiangling, executing him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He cut Huan Xuan down, then killed Huan Shikang, Huan Jun, and Yu Yizhi. Huan Sheng was taken to Jiangling and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 乘輿返正於江陵，以毛修之為驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned to correctness at Jiangling; Mao Xiuzhi was made Valiant Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was restored at Jiangling. Mao Xiuzhi was made Valiant Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 甲申，大赦，諸以畏逼從逆者一無所問。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, a great amnesty—all who followed the rebellion from fear and compulsion were not questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen a general amnesty was proclaimed; those who had followed the usurper under duress were not punished.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，奉神主於太廟。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, the spirit tablets were reverently placed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the ancestral tablets were restored to the Imperial Temple.

sentences.zh: 劉毅等傳送玄首，梟於大桁。。

translations.literal: Liu Yi and the others transmitted and escorted Xuan's head; it was displayed on a pole at Daheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi sent Huan Xuan's head to the capital, where it was spiked on the Daheng gate.

sentences.zh: 毅等既戰勝，以為大事已定，不急追躡，又遇風，船未能進，玄死幾一旬，諸軍猶未至。

translations.literal: Yi and the others, having already won the battle, thought the great affair was settled and did not press in pursuit; they also met wind, and the ships could not advance. Nearly a ten-day period after Xuan's death, the various armies still had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After their victory, Liu Yi and his colleagues assumed the war was over and did not pursue in haste. Contrary winds held their fleet back, and nearly ten days after Huan Xuan's death their forces had still not come up.

sentences.zh: 時桓謙匿於沮中，揚武將軍醒振匿於華容浦，玄故將王稚徽戍巴陵，遣人報振云「桓歆已克京邑，馮稚復克尋陽，劉毅諸軍並中路敗退。」

translations.literal: At the time Huan Qian was hiding in Ju, the General Who Displays Martiality Huan Zhen was hiding at Huarong Ford, and Xuan's former officer Wang Zhihui was garrisoning Baling. He sent someone to report to Zhen, saying, "Huan Xin has already taken the capital; Feng Zhi has again taken Xunyang; Liu Yi and the various armies have all been defeated on the central route and are retreating."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian lay hidden in Ju, while Huan Zhen, General Who Displays Martiality, concealed himself at Huarong Ford. Huan Xuan's old officer Wang Zhihui held Baling and sent word to Zhen that Huan Xin had seized the capital, Feng Zhi had retaken Xunyang, and Liu Yi's armies had all been routed on the middle road and were falling back.

sentences.zh: 振大喜，聚黨得二百人，襲江陵，桓謙亦聚眾應之。

translations.literal: Zhen was greatly pleased, gathered followers to the number of two hundred men, and raided Jiangling; Huan Qian also raised troops to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was overjoyed. He mustered two hundred men and struck at Jiangling, and Huan Qian rallied his own followers to join the attack.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己丑，復陷江陵，殺王康產、王騰之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day jichou, they again took Jiangling and killed Wang Kangchan and Wang Tengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the day jichou, they seized Jiangling again and put Wang Kangchan and Wang Tengzhi to death.

sentences.zh: 振見帝於行宮，躍馬奮戈，直至階下，問桓昇所在。

translations.literal: Zhen saw the Emperor at the traveling palace, leaped his horse and brandished his halberd straight to the foot of the steps, and asked where Huan Sheng was.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rode into the temporary palace, spurred his horse forward with halberd raised, and halted at the foot of the steps to demand where Huan Sheng was.

sentences.zh: 聞其已死，瞋目謂帝曰：「臣門戶何負國家，而屠滅若是！」」

translations.literal: Learning he was already dead, he glared and said to the Emperor: "What has my clan owed the state, that slaughter like this should be done!"
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Sheng was already dead, he glared at the Emperor and cried, "What crime has my house committed against the realm, that you should butcher us so!"

sentences.zh: 琅邪王德文下床謂曰：「此豈我兄弟意邪！」

translations.literal: The Prince of Langya, Dewen, stepped down from the bed and said: "Surely this was not my brothers' intent!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dewen of Langya rose from the couch and said, "Surely this was never my brothers' wish!"

sentences.zh: 振欲殺帝，謙苦禁之，乃下馬，斂容致拜而出。

translations.literal: Zhen wished to kill the Emperor; Qian strenuously forbade him, whereupon he dismounted, composed his countenance, performed a bow, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen meant to kill the Emperor, but Qian pleaded with him until he relented. Zhen then dismounted, composed his face, bowed formally, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，振為玄舉哀，立喪庭，謚曰武悼皇帝。。

translations.literal: On day renchen, Zhen held mourning for Xuan, established a mourning hall, and gave the posthumous title Emperor Wudao.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Zhen mourned Huan Xuan, set up a mourning hall, and gave him the posthumous title Emperor Wudao.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，謙等帥群臣奉璽綬於帝曰：「主上法堯禪舜，今楚祚不終，百姓之心復歸於晉矣。」

translations.literal: On day guisi, Qian led the ministers in presenting the seal and cord to the Emperor, saying: "Your Majesty followed Yao's model in yielding to Shun; now Chu's fortune does not complete its course, and the hearts of the people have returned to Jin."
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Qian led the court in presenting the imperial seal and cord to the Emperor, saying, "Your Majesty followed Yao in yielding the throne to Shun; the house of Chu has run its course, and the people's hearts have returned to Jin."

sentences.zh: 以琅邪王德文領徐州刺史，振為都督八州諸軍事、荊州刺史，謙復為侍中、衛將軍，加江、豫二州刺史，帝侍御左右，皆振心腹也。。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langya Dewen was made Inspector of Xuzhou; Zhen was made Grand Marshal over the Military Affairs of Eight Provinces and Inspector of Jingzhou; Qian was again made Palace Attendant and Guards General with the added offices of Inspectors of Jiang and Yu; those attending the Emperor on left and right were all Zhen's trusted men.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dewen of Langya was named Inspector of Xuzhou; Zhen became commander of military affairs in eight provinces and Inspector of Jingzhou; Qian was restored as Palace Attendant and Guards General and given Jiang and Yu as well. Every attendant at the Emperor's side was one of Zhen's own men.

sentences.zh: 振少薄行，玄不以子姪齒之。

translations.literal: Zhen in youth had poor conduct; Xuan did not rank him among his sons and nephews as an equal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had been dissolute in his youth, and Huan Xuan had never treated him as the equal of his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 至是，歎曰：「公昔不早用我，遂致此敗。

translations.literal: At this time he sighed and said: "You, Uncle, did not employ me early, and thus brought on this defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Now he sighed and said, "Uncle, if you had used me sooner, we would never have come to this ruin.

sentences.zh: 若使公在，我為前鋒，天下不足定也。

translations.literal: If you, Uncle, were still alive and I served as vanguard, securing the realm would not have been difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Had you lived and put me at the van, pacifying the realm would have been no great matter.

sentences.zh: 今獨作此，安歸乎？」

translations.literal: Now acting alone as I do, where shall I go?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that I stand alone, where can I turn?"

sentences.zh: 遂縱意酒色，肆行誅殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he indulged wine and women at will and carried out executions at random.
translations.idiomatic: He gave himself over to wine and women and killed at whim.

sentences.zh: 謙勸振引兵下戰，己守江陵，振素輕謙，不從其言。。

translations.literal: Qian urged Zhen to lead troops down to fight while he himself held Jiangling; Zhen had always looked down on Qian and did not heed his words.
translations.idiomatic: Qian urged Zhen to take the field in person while he held Jiangling, but Zhen had always despised Qian and refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 劉毅至巴陵，誅王稚徽。

translations.literal: Liu Yi reached Baling and executed Wang Zhihui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi reached Baling and executed Wang Zhihui.

sentences.zh: 何無忌、劉道規進攻桓謙於馬頭，桓蔚於龍泉，皆破之。

translations.literal: He Wuji and Liu Daogui attacked Huan Qian at Matou and Huan Wei at Longquan, defeating both.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji and Liu Daogui attacked Huan Qian at Matou and Huan Wei at Longquan and defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 蔚，秘之子也。。

translations.literal: Wei was Mi's son.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was the son of Huan Mi.

sentences.zh: 無忌欲乘勝直趣江陵，道規曰：「兵法屈申有時，不可苟進。

translations.literal: Wuji wished to press the victory and go straight to Jiangling. Daogui said: "In the art of war, bending and extending have their seasons; one must not advance rashly.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji wanted to follow up the victory and drive straight on Jiangling. Liu Daogui said, "In war, advance and delay each have their season; we must not rush forward blindly.

sentences.zh: 諸桓世居西楚，群下皆為竭力；

translations.literal: The various Huans for generations have dwelt in Western Chu, and their followers all exert themselves to the utmost for them;
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clan has ruled Western Chu for generations, and every man under them will fight to the last;

sentences.zh: 振勇冠三軍，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: Zhen's courage leads the three armies; he is hard to contend with at the point of the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's valor is unmatched in the host, and he is not a foe to meet head-on.

sentences.zh: 且可息兵養銳，徐以計策縻之，不憂不克。」

translations.literal: For the present we may rest the troops and nurture sharpness, and slowly use stratagems to tether them; there is no worry of not overcoming."
translations.idiomatic: Let us rest the army and sharpen our edge, then wear them down with stratagem. Victory need not worry us."

sentences.zh: 無忌不從。

translations.literal: Wuji did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 振逆戰於靈溪，馮該以兵會之，無忌等大敗，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Zhen met them in battle at Ling Stream; Feng Gai came with troops to join him; Wuji and the others suffered a great defeat, with more than a thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen gave battle at Ling Stream. Feng Gai came up with reinforcements, and He Wuji's force was shattered, with more than a thousand dead.

sentences.zh: 退還尋陽，與劉毅等上箋請罪。

translations.literal: They withdrew to Xunyang and, with Liu Yi and the others, submitted memorials begging forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: They fell back to Xunyang and, together with Liu Yi, sent memorials asking pardon for their defeat.

sentences.zh: 劉容以毅節度諸軍，免其青州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Rong put Yi in command of the armies and removed him from office as Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong placed Liu Yi in overall command of the armies but stripped him of the Qingzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 桓振以桓蔚為雍州刺史，鎮襄陽。。

translations.literal: Huan Zhen made Huan Wei Inspector of Yongzhou, stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen appointed Huan Wei Inspector of Yongzhou and posted him at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 柳約之、羅述、甄季之聞桓玄死，自白帝進軍，至枝江，聞何無忌等敗於靈溪，亦引兵退，俄而述、季之皆病，約之詣桓振偽降，欲謀襲振，事洩，振殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Yuezhi, Luo Shu, and Zhen Jizhi, hearing Huan Xuan was dead, advanced from Baidi to Zhijiang. Hearing He Wuji and the others had been defeated at Ling Stream, they also withdrew their troops. Shortly Shu and Jizhi both fell ill. Yuezhi went to Huan Zhen in feigned surrender, intending to plot a surprise attack on Zhen; the affair leaked out, and Zhen killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuezhi, Luo Shu, and Zhen Jizhi heard that Huan Xuan was dead, they marched from Baidi toward Zhijiang. Learning of He Wuji's defeat at Ling Stream, they pulled back. Soon Shu and Jizhi fell ill. Yuezhi went to Zhen pretending to submit, planning to strike him by surprise; the plot was discovered, and Zhen had him killed.

sentences.zh: 約之司馬時延祖、涪陵太守文處茂收其餘眾，保涪陵。。

translations.literal: Yuezhi's marshal Shi Yanzu and the Fuling Prefect Wen Chumao gathered the remaining troops and held Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi's marshal Shi Yanzu and the prefect of Fuling, Wen Chumao, gathered the survivors and held Fuling.

sentences.zh: 六月，毛璩遣將攻漢中，斬桓希，璩自領梁州。。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Mao Jin sent generals to attack Hanzhong, beheaded Huan Xi, and Jin himself took charge of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Mao Jin sent generals against Hanzhong, slew Huan Xi, and took Liangzhou for himself.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，戊申，永安皇后何氏崩。。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on day wushen, Empress He of Yong'an died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on wushen, Empress He of Yong'an died.

sentences.zh: 燕苻昭儀有疾，龍城人王榮自言能療之。

translations.literal: In Yan, Lady Fu the Honored Consort had an illness; Wang Rong of Longcheng declared himself able to cure it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan, Lady Fu the Honored Consort fell ill, and Wang Rong of Longcheng claimed he could heal her.

sentences.zh: 昭儀卒，燕王熙立榮於公車門，支解而焚之。。

translations.literal: The Honored Consort died. The King of Yan Xi had Rong set up at the Gate of the Public Chariot, dismembered him, and burned him.
translations.idiomatic: When the consort died, King Xi of Yan had Rong bound at the Gate of the Public Chariot, cut him limb from limb, and burned the pieces.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸酉，葬穆章皇后於永平陵。。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day guiyou, they buried Empress Muzhang at Yongping Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guiyou, Empress Muzhang was interred at Yongping Tomb.

sentences.zh: 魏置六謁官，准古六卿。。

translations.literal: Wei established six yeguan offices, matching the ancient Six Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei created six yeguan offices, modeled on the ancient Six Ministers.

sentences.zh: 九月，刁騁謀反，伏誅，刁氏遂亡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Diao Chi plotted rebellion, was executed, and the Diao clan thereupon perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Diao Chi rebelled, was put to death, and the house of Diao was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 刁氏素富，奴客縱橫，專固山澤，為京口之患。

translations.literal: The Diao clan had long been wealthy; their slave-retainers ranged freely and monopolized the mountains and marshes, becoming a scourge of Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: The Diaos had long been immensely rich. Their bondsmen and clients ranged unchecked, holding the hills and marshes by force, and had become a plague on Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 劉裕散其資蓄，令民稱力而取之，彌日不盡。

translations.literal: Liu Yu distributed their stored wealth, ordering the people to take it according to their strength; a whole day did not exhaust it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu opened their hoards to the people, letting each take what he could carry, and a full day was not enough to empty them.

sentences.zh: 時州郡饑弊，民賴之以濟。。

translations.literal: At the time the provinces and commanderies were famine-stricken and impoverished; the people relied on this to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces were starving and destitute, and countless families lived on that windfall.

sentences.zh: 乞伏乾歸及楊盛戰於竹嶺，為盛所敗。。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui and Yang Sheng fought at Zhuling; Gangui was defeated by Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui fought Yang Sheng at Zhuling and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 西涼公暠立子歆為世子。。

translations.literal: The Duke of Western Liang Gao installed his son Xin as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, Duke of Western Liang, named his son Xin heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 魏主珪臨昭陽殿改補百官，引朝臣文武，親加銓擇，隨才授任。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler Gui came to Zhaoyang Hall to revise and fill the hundred offices, summoned the civil and military courtiers, personally weighed and chose them, and appointed each according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler Tuoba Gui sat in Zhaoyang Hall to reorganize the bureaucracy, summoned civil and military officials, personally weighed their merits, and assigned each post to fit his ability.

sentences.zh: 列爵四等：王封大郡，公封小郡，侯封大縣，伯封小縣。

translations.literal: He ranked nobility in four grades: kings were enfeoffed with large commanderies, dukes with small commanderies, marquises with large counties, and earls with small counties.
translations.idiomatic: He defined four ranks of nobility: kings received great commanderies, dukes lesser commanderies, marquises great counties, and earls lesser counties.

sentences.zh: 其品第一至第四，舊臣有功無爵者追封之，宗室疏遠及異姓襲封者降爵有差。

translations.literal: For ranks first through fourth, old ministers with merit but no nobility were ennobled retroactively; collateral and distant clansmen and alien surnames inheriting enfeoffments had their nobility reduced by graded steps.
translations.idiomatic: For ranks one through four, veteran ministers who had earned merit but held no title were ennobled posthumously or belatedly, while distant kinsmen of the imperial clan and non-Tuoba heirs had their inherited ranks reduced by fixed degrees.

sentences.zh: 又置散官五等，其品第五至第九；

translations.literal: He also established five grades of unsalaried office, ranks fifth through ninth;
translations.idiomatic: He also created five grades of unsalaried office, ranks five through nine;

sentences.zh: 文官造士才能秀異、武官堪為將帥者，其品亦比第五至第九；

translations.literal: civil officials of accomplished learning with outstanding talent and military officers fit to be generals and commanders were also ranked fifth through ninth;
translations.idiomatic: scholar-officials of proven talent and soldiers fit for high command were likewise classed from rank five to nine;

sentences.zh: 百官有闕，則取於其中以補之。

translations.literal: when any of the hundred offices had a vacancy, men were taken from among these to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: and whenever a regular post fell vacant, appointees were drawn from these pools to fill it.

sentences.zh: 其官名多不用漢、魏之舊，仿上古龍官、鳥官，謂諸曹之使為鳧鴨，取其飛之迅疾也；

translations.literal: Most office names did not use Han and Wei precedents but imitated the ancient Dragon Offices and Bird Offices. He called the messengers of the various bureaus "wild duck" and "mallard," taking their swift flight;
translations.idiomatic: Most titles abandoned Han and Wei usage and echoed antiquity's Dragon and Bird offices. Couriers of the ministries were called Wild Duck and Mallard, for the speed of their flight;

sentences.zh: 謂候官伺察者為白鷺，取其延頸遠望也；

translations.literal: he called surveillance officers "white egret," taking their stretching the neck to gaze far;
translations.idiomatic: inspectors were named White Egret, for the bird's long-necked watchfulness;

sentences.zh: 餘皆類此。。

translations.literal: the rest were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: and the rest followed the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇南海，攻番禺。

translations.literal: Lu Xun raided Nanhai and attacked Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun raided Nanhai and laid siege to Panyu.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史濮陽吳隱之拒守百餘日。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Guangzhou, Wu Yinzhi of Puyang, held out in defense for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yinzhi of Puyang, Inspector of Guangzhou, held the city for more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬戌，循夜襲城而陷之，燒府捨、民室俱盡，執吳隱之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on day renxu, Xun raided the city by night and took it, burning government buildings and commoners' houses entirely, and seized Wu Yinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on renxu, Xun stormed the city by night and took it. Government halls and private houses burned to the ground, and Wu Yinzhi was captured.

sentences.zh: 循自稱平南將軍，攝廣州事。

translations.literal: Xun styled himself General Who Pacifies the South and took charge of Guangzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xun styled himself General Who Pacifies the South and assumed control of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 聚燒骨為共塚，葬於洲上，得髑髏三萬餘枚。

translations.literal: He gathered the burned bones into a common tomb and buried them on the islet; skulls obtained numbered more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He heaped the charred bones into a common mound on the river islet and counted more than thirty thousand skulls.

sentences.zh: 又使徐道覆攻始興，執始興相阮腆之。。

translations.literal: He also sent Xu Daofu to attack Shixing and seized the Shixing chancellor Ruan Tianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xu Daofu against Shixing and took its chief minister Ruan Tianzhi prisoner.

sentences.zh: 劉容領青州刺史。

translations.literal: Liu Rong took charge as Inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rong assumed the Qingzhou inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 劉敬宣在尋陽，聚糧繕船，未嘗無備，故何無忌等雖敗退，賴以復振。

translations.literal: Liu Jingxuan was at Xunyang, gathering grain and repairing ships, never without preparation; therefore although He Wuji and the others were defeated and withdrew, they relied on this to recover and revive.
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang, Liu Jingxuan stockpiled grain and refitted ships and was never caught unprepared, so when He Wuji and the others were beaten back they were able to rally on his base.

sentences.zh: 桓玄兄子亮自稱江州刺史，寇豫章，敬宣擊破之。。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan's elder brother's son Liang styled himself Inspector of Jiangzhou, raided Yuzhang, and Jingxuan attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Liang, a nephew of Huan Xuan, styled himself Inspector of Jiangzhou and raided Yuzhang, but Jingxuan routed him.

sentences.zh: 劉毅、何無忌、劉道規復自尋陽西上，至夏口。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, He Wuji, and Liu Daogui again went west from Xunyang and reached Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, He Wuji, and Liu Daogui marched west again from Xunyang and reached Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 桓振遣鎮東將軍馮該守東岸，揚武將軍孟山圖據魯山城，輔國將軍桓仙客守偃月壘，眾合萬人，水陸相援。

translations.literal: Huan Zhen sent the General Who Pacifies the East Feng Gai to hold the eastern bank, the General Who Displays Martiality Meng Shantu to hold Lucheng Mountain, and the General Who Assists the State Huan Xianke to hold Crescent Fortress. Their forces together numbered ten thousand men, supporting one another by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen posted Feng Gai, General Who Pacifies the East, on the eastern shore, Meng Shantu, General Who Displays Martiality, on Lucheng Mountain, and Huan Xianke, General Who Assists the State, at Crescent Fortress. Their combined strength was ten thousand men, linked by land and river.
